h1: Coaching Workshop for Leaders and Managers
content:
Designed to create real impact at work, our coaching workshop equips leaders and managers with a stronger mindset, better management capabilities, and practical tools they can apply in everyday workplace situations.

Why Leaders Today Must Adopt a Coaching Mindset

Leadership is evolving from directive management to a coaching-centred approach grounded in research. Leaders who adopt this mindset do not merely "manage" employees; they architect environments that foster higher engagement and more open communication.

Instead of simply giving instructions, these leaders develop other employees through active listening, powerful questioning, and constructive feedback. Our coaching workshop equips leaders with these essential competencies through real workplace scenarios, and guided practice that can be immediately applied on the job.

Designed for Leaders and Managers Who Want to Lead with Impact

  • Develop a coaching mindset by integrating coaching competencies into managerial roles. This workshop is ideal for emerging leaders, mid-level managers, senior leaders, and HR or L&D professionals responsible for guiding teams and driving organizational growth.
  • Beyond theory, this hands-on course for leaders and managers provides real-world coaching applications, case studies, and expert guidance that prepare them to become Coaching-Leaders. The skills learned in this workshop are especially valuable for improving team performance, navigating change management, and enhancing day-to-day communication and collaboration.

By completing this coaching workshop, your organization can enhance its leadership capabilities and earn a recognition certification - Certified Coaching-Leader, positioning them as a forward-thinking leader who drives measurable success.

Become a Certified Coaching Leader - Elevate Your Leadership Practice

Strengthen Your Organization’s Coaching Culture and Capability

As the pace of business quickens and competition stiffens, organizations and their leaders continue to ask, "how can we achieve a significant and sustainable competitive advantage?"

The world's top-performing companies recognize that developing leaders in coaching is a key driver of organizational success. Training leaders in coaching builds a culture of continuous learning, enhances team performance, improves communication, and increases employee engagement and retention. Engaged employees are committed to the organization's success, willing to go the extra mile, more productive, and stay longer with the organization.

"The best companies now know, without a doubt, where productivity comes from. It comes from challenged, empowered, excited, and rewarded teams. It comes from engaging every single mind in the organisation, making everyone part of the action, and allowing everyone to have a voice - a role – in the success of the enterprise. Doing so raises productivity, not incrementally, but by multiples." Jack Welch, former CEO and Chairman, General Electric

As complexity continues to infiltrate every aspect of the organization, leaders trained in coaching through our workshops ensure people work more effectively and efficiently, enabling the organization to achieve measurable business results and maintain a competitive edge.

What You Will Learn in This Coaching Workshop

What makes this workshop truly unique is that it offers leaders the opportunity to develop coaching competencies traditionally reserved for professional coaching certification. As an ICF-accredited coach training program, this course is part of a professional coaching certification pathway, meaning leaders and managers can now gain the same level of coaching proficiency as those training to become professional coaches.

This isn't just a leadership training program but also a transformational experience that empowers leaders to think like a professional coach when leading their team, elevating their ability to inspire, guide, and drive meaningful change.

By completing this workshop, leaders develop a coaching mindset and integrate coaching competencies into their leadership and managerial roles. Key topics and skills covered include:

  • Coaching Mindset: Cultivating the curiosity and self-awareness required to lead with intention.
  • Practical Coaching Tools: Applying frameworks like Awareness-Clarity-Choice to guide problem-solving, decision-making, and team development.
  • Empathy and Emotional Intelligence (EQ): Navigating the emotions of the "protective mind" to promote psychological safety.
  • Feedback Conversations: Delivering high-stakes feedback that motivates vertical growth.
  • Conflict Navigation: Navigating "threshold" conversations to turn friction into collaborative opportunity.
  • ICF Core Competencies Application: Maintaining the professional rigor and ethical boundaries of a master practitioner.

The good news is that we have expertise in advanced instructional design to customize the learning to fit your organization’s culture or learning goals, helping to boost your organization’s coaching capacity and drive measurable impact across teams.

Why “Leading with Impact” is Essential for Your Leadership Development Program

“Leading with Impact” is a crucial component of any leadership development program because it equips managers with the coaching skills needed to succeed in today’s evolving workplace.

By learning to coach, managers become leaders who can engage, inspire, and positively influence their teams. As a result, this shift strengthens talent management, boosts learning agility, and drives higher levels of performance across individuals and teams. In a workforce that values connection, empowerment, and growth, coaching becomes an essential people skill for effective leadership.

Moreover, this workshop focuses on practical coaching techniques that help leaders ask the questions that uncover root causes, spark insight, and drive ownership. By adopting a coaching style over a directive approach, leaders build stronger engagement and accountability, leading to improved productivity and better business outcomes. These capabilities clearly set highly effective leaders apart from average managers.

Built on a proprietary transformational coaching approach and supported by the science of positive leadership, this workshop provides leaders with a facilitative framework that encourages better thinking and meaningful development. Over time, this training leads to sustainable behavior change, stronger performance management, and long-term organizational success, highlighting that coaching is a key driver of modern leadership effectiveness.

Organizational Benefits: From Engagement to Performance

It is people, not organizational structures or systems, that drive growth. Hence, leaders and managers need to master skills that inspire commitment and accountability.

As Stephen Denning highlights in "The Secret Language of Leadership", leaders create impact by generating enthusiasm and communicating in ways that truly resonate. In this context, the coaching workshop becomes more than a methodology or trend. It is a leadership approach that strengthens how leaders connect, communicate, and motivate, making training more impactful and results-driven.

Organizations that institutionalize this level of coaching see stronger team cohesion, higher engagement, and fewer interpersonal conflicts. Because coaching conversations encourage employees to think through challenges rather than just follow instructions, they develop ownership and problem-solving ability.

This leads to improved productivity, more consistent performance, and a stronger leadership pipeline as emerging leaders step up with confidence.

Coaching in Action - Practice, Feedback & Real-World Application

To ensure learning translates into real workplace impact, this workshop emphasizes hands-on practice and real coaching conversations. Leaders engage in structured role-plays, peer-coaching exercises, and guided practice sessions that mirror real leadership scenarios.

Learners also receive constructive feedback from facilitators and peers, helping them refine their communication style, questioning techniques, and listening skills. Leaders leave with the confidence to immediately apply these approaches, ensuring sustainable behavior change and stronger leadership performance.

Flexible Delivery Options – Online and Hybrid Workshops

Our coaching workshop is designed for maximum flexibility to suit your organization’s needs, offering online and hybrid sessions that fit easily into your schedule.

To make participation even more convenient for geographically dispersed teams, our monthly training calendar automatically converts session times to your local time zone, so you can join when it works best for you.

Speak to a Leadership Coaching Expert – Book a Consultation

Modern workplaces demand sharper performance, smarter collaboration, and teams that consistently deliver results. Our coaching workshop for leaders and managers is designed to meet these expectations by building practical leadership and coaching capabilities that translate directly into workplace impact.

Our Certified Professional Coaches bring extensive corporate experience and work closely with you to design a leadership training workshop that aligns with your organization’s specific goals and challenges.

title: Distinctiveness of our Transformational Approach-Coach Masters Academy
content:
The Distinctiveness of our Transformational Approach

Coaching has become the most sought after solution for talent-development strategy in many organizations, ensuring that high-potential employees and new leaders have the tools they need to rapidly adapt to their roles and assimilate into the organization’s unique culture. The increased demand for professional coaching undoubtedly reflects a basic human desire for deep connection and reflection. One way to develop people and advance their potential is to offer them the right balance of challenge and growth support.

The question we are asking now is what kind of coaching process will enable a change that is sustainable in nature?

Re-think the way you are coaching

Professional coaching is a service in which a trained coach helps people to clarify their goals and intentions, work towards them, and overcome obstacles to their realization. To enable sustainable change requires awareness and a thorough thinking process - it is not something we get at the click of a mouse. A Professional Coach guides individuals on this learning journey where they deepen their understanding and walk away with greater clarity. Watch the 90 seconds video explaining how our transformative coaching enables deep and sustainable change.

The concept of transformation is often considered the most complete or radical form of change. “Trans” means to go across or to move from one stage to another, suggesting a change in form. It involves a dynamic change in nature, not just a surface-level change. 

Impactful coaching that results in a sustainable change requires people first to gain awareness of how they perceive their reality. They need to bring this awareness to the forefront of their minds, allowing them to make considered decisions that truly align with their priorities. It is not enough for people to walk away from the coaching session with only a short-term “solution”. 

Each person holds so much power within themselves that needs to be let out. Sometimes they just need a little nudge, a little direction, a little support, and the greatest things can happen. Pete Carroll.

The coaching conversation needs to encourage deep reflection, which empowers people to jettison thoughts, perspectives, and emotions that are no longer relevant, and learn new ones. As such, the ACC Conversation provides people with an expansive space in which to examine how they respond to their situation through reflective inquiry. 

Moving from Tactical to Adaptive to Generative Change

The ACC Conversation is transformational because it questions the integrity of deeply held assumptions based on prior experiences. It gives people a fresh lens on how they construct and perceive their situation and through the transformative process, guide them to assess their value system and worldview. It also offers people an expanded space for self-discovery and uses the emerging understanding that unfolds in the conversation to support them to make empowering choices in moving forward.

It is interesting to note that people rarely take time to consider how they are thinking. Instead, they focus their attention on the “what” aspects, such as “what do I need to do” and “what are the barriers to my goals”. Consequently, the vast majority of their actions and decisions are merely a reactive response to the situation that either attempts to fix or resolve something.

Here is an important question that we need to ask ourselves:

when the goal is to advance human potential, will a tactical approach offer sufficient guidance to people working to generate higher levels of well-being and development?

Delivering impactful results requires us to be deliberate in choosing approaches that best match the context.

Tactical change is of course ideal when both the problem and the expected outcome are clearly defined. Current ways of thinking are generally adequate for the task, and needed skillsets can be learned. Engaging people at this level of change supports them in creating adaptive change to manage the situation. 
But this is where understanding the distinct difference between tactical and generative change makes a difference.

Being able to solve a problem or putting something in place is not the same as moving forward. And that’s where generative change comes in. 

Generative change means creating something beyond what already exists. It is not merely a cosmetic change, but a shift that allows new levels of mastery, which enable you to achieve entirely new outcomes. This is an important process that connects learning agility and sustainability. 

The process of experiencing generative change deepens our learning and increases our capacity to apply the new understanding in a new context. When we can adapt faster and navigate complex situations more easily, we become more resilient and vigilant; and, subsequently, we can engage in sustainable change.

This is the testimony by Karen, HR Director sharing her personal coaching experience as a client.

What I appreciated most about this conversation is the coach's safe, open, and expansive space. It expanded my mind to uncover my inner felt need - a need for certainty - that is hidden behind my concern. This shift in my understanding is so refreshing and empowering, and most importantly, it enabled me to move forward boldly to deal with the situation. 

What is so unique about this coaching approach? I noticed that the coach helped me get out of my logical thought process loop and actually right to the matter's heart. The questions asked caused me to be very reflective instead of answering "reason". I was able to realize new insights and also recognize connections between my own thoughts and my feelings. The process is so organic and powerful.

How is this coaching different from your past coaching experiences? I have had a few coaching sessions in the past, and when comparing them to this session, I would now say that they are more of consulting types of coaching.  In those sessions, the coaching focuses more on the details and facts about my topic to create strategies to resolve the situation. I walked away with an "action plan", but not experiencing a true "transformation". This session has enabled me with insights that I could not have realized on my own and are far more impactful as they have changed the way I viewed my situation.

A reflective inquiry process that heightens the self-awareness

Reflective learning is our ability to pause and examine our thought process, construct meaning, look for connection, and unpack our thoughts.

A generative change is a systemic concept of a whole that consists of interconnected parts; it is based in part on the premise that a small change can create or facilitate considerable change. This is where transformative learning occurs, and the nature of the change people experience is often a deep, fundamental revision to their beliefs, principles and feelings. This allows them to modify their understanding of themselves and others, as well as their sense of what’s possible.

The theory of transformative learning is the core principle of the ACC Conversation.

Transformative learning occurs when learning results in a change in an individual’s frame of reference. These reference frames are the cognitive building blocks that we use to understand our world and influence our values, attitudes, and associated behaviours. When people apply critical self-reflection to consider their interpretations, beliefs, and experiences, they become able to transform their reference frames. This process is known as perspective transformation, and it involves experiencing a profound, structural shift in basic premises of thought, feelings, and action.

Our transformative coaching offers you a robust framework that can be applied in a wide and diverse context including coaching executives in workplace, leadership effectiveness and development and career-related issues. It can also be used in life coaching for people seeking fulfilment, purpose, meaning and alignment.

The Coherence Integration Practitioner certification is designed for practitioners who want to strengthen the quality of how they work with people — whether in coaching, facilitation, leadership, mentoring, education, or other people-development roles.
This program develops your capacity to work with heart-brain coherence as a practical, trainable inner resource. You will learn how to bring greater steadiness, clarity, and congruence into the way you listen, respond, and support others through complexity and change.
What this training offers: 
  • A grounded understanding of brain–heart coherence and the inner conditions that support it.
  • A practitioner-focused approach to using coherence as a capacity, not just a technique.
  • Practical tools to help people access greater clarity, regulation, and purposeful action.
  • A broader way of working that strengthens your presence, perception, and impact.

Why it matters: When people are under pressure, insight alone is often not enough. This training helps you support the inner conditions that enable clearer thinking, better self-regulation, and more aligned action.

Who it is for. This program is for coaches, facilitators, leaders, mentors, educators, and other professionals who want to deepen their support for people in real-world contexts.

Develop the inner capacity to meet complexity with clarity, presence, and purposeful action.

This program is ICF Level 1 Accredited and meets the requirements for the ACC Credential.

The Foundational Advantage Coaching Program is ideal for those who want to formalise their coaching competencies, develop industry-aligned skills, or explore coaching as a potential professional pathway — even without prior experience.

Throughout the programme, you’ll be supported by faculty who are deeply committed to your growth — both as a coach and as a person. Learning is paced, reflective, and practical, with clear frameworks, real coaching practice, and personalised feedback woven throughout.

Course Fee: Early Bird NZD 4,900 ends 9 Oct I Standard Price: NZD 5,900
Includes morning/afternoon tea & lunch during the in-person session days.

Meet Your Facilitators

This programme is led by two experienced Coach Educators who bring depth, clarity, and heart to your learning journey.

Annekarien van de Velde (Master Certified Coach). A senior faculty team with extensive experience training coaches and leaders in Aotearoa New Zealand and internationally. Known for her warm, grounded presence, Annekarien specialise in coaching mindset, self-awareness, and high-quality coaching conversations that translate theory into confident, embodied practice.

Kiri McCrae (Professional Certified Coach) brings a relational and culturally grounded perspective to the programme. Drawing on Maori worldviews, Kiri supports learners to explore coaching through connection, values, and relational wealth.


Program Overview


Learning Lab I 4 - 6 Nov 2026 I Auckland, New Zealand
Being onsite adds a special depth to the experience — you’ll practise together, receive real-time feedback, and learn from each other in a dynamic, engaging environment. It truly brings the material to life. You will deepen your understanding of core coaching theories and practices.


Practical Lab I 12 sessions from 9 Nov 2026 to 29 Jan 2027 I Online
Mix & match the options below to complete at least 10 sessions.
Mondays & Tuesdays I 7–9 PM NZT 
Tuesdays & Wednesdays I 11:30 AM – 12:30 PM NZT
You’ll rotate through the roles of coach, client, and observer, gaining confidence, structure, and real coaching experience.


Mentoring Lab I 3 Sessions I Online
Receive personalised guidance and developmental feedback from your mentor.
Requirements:
- Submit a recorded coaching session and transcript before each meeting (ICF standard)
- Schedule mentoring sessions directly with your mentor at mutually suitable times


Enrichment Lab I 3 Sessions I Online
Enhance your learning through live coaching demonstrations led by experienced faculty and growth-focused webinars. A brief reflection is submitted via the LMS after each session.

Once the form is submitted, our team will arrange a brief conversation with you.

This allows us to confirm alignment, clarify expectations, and provide the full program details along with the regionally appropriate course fee.

Or you can book an appointment and speak with our friendly team to learn more about the program.

title: Employee Engagement Training-Coach Masters Academy
h1: What makes Coach Masters Academy your preferred choice?
content:
Transformative Coaching : Enabling Sustainable Change

  • 1st Level Training: Core Training for Professional Coaching
  • Training Format: 3 Days In-Persons + 10 Online Practical Coaching

Achieve Personal Mastery and Obtain Professional Credential

Upon completing the coach training course, you will walk away with 75 hours of ICF approved coach training under the ASCTH accredited program. You will receive the certification as a Certified Professional Coach that qualify you to apply for the ICF Membership and/or Credential. * Most importantly, you will acquire the coaching competency to enable people experience powerful shift in their thinking.

What Makes Coach Masters Academy Your Preferred Choice

* we also offer bundle package that includes the mentoring coaching requires for credential application; please email us for more details.

Transformative Coaching: Enabling Sustainable Change

In additional to the brochure, you can also download a compilation of invaluable articles contributed by world-leading Master Certified Coach
DOWNLOAD BROCHURE

Coach Masters Academy is committed to delivering the highest standard of coaching training. With more than a thousand coaches and leaders completing their training with us across the globe each year, we offer a training package that includes:

Global Learning Platform

Immerse yourself in a global learning experience and grow your international coaching network through our expanding alumni which spans across the globe.

  • Connect with coaches and leaders worldwide and develop a global coaching network for collaboration
  • Experience rich, diverse and cross-cultural learning and prepares yourself as a global citizen
  • Offer pro-bono coaching through our Success And You Foundation and accumulate coaching experience

Comprehensive Instructional Design

Accelerated your learning with carefully designed Learning Lab, Practical Lab, Practicum, Peer to Peer Support and Coaching Supervision to develop your coaching competency.

  • Manage your learning progress a eLearning platform with our Learning Management System (LMS) to manage progress, share and receive feedback.
  • Gain access to a library of invaluable learning resources, coaching tools and templates for business practice.
  • Build your coaching practices with our Business Development Program

Continual Professional Development

Well crafted and properly delivered continuing professional development to help you remain competent and relevance.

  • Offer extensive post-training support through our monthly learning webinars and live coaching demonstrations
  • Provide teaching platform as a Student Mentor to support new students in their learning journey.
  • Earn Continual Coach Education (CCE) units for your ICF credential renewal through our strategic partnership with Asia Pacific Association of Coaches (APAC).

Our Learning Experiences

We have successfully trained thousands of leaders and coaches across the globe using our proprietary transformative coaching to help our clients to achieve sustainable results. Hear what our graduates shared their learning experiences with us.

An amazing program that truly creates space and creativity for people to be empowered with the knowledge they already possess inside. A life-changing experience. I would highly recommend it for anybody influencing leaders or looking to create positive change in people.

Amy Styles

National Training Manager | New Zealand

CMA maintains a high standard in the delivery with useful materials, impactful videos, and lots of opportunities for reflection and practice. The learning through listening to coaching conversation follows by in-depth discussion provides a rich resource that helps us to map theory with application and I find it to be extremely invaluable accelerating our competencies. The academy also provides many good platforms for post-training learning where we can learn from various Supervisors across the globe. It allows me to apply my skills outside the classroom learning context.

Elvin Tay

Senior Learning Consultant | Singapore

The Master Trainer is an amazing individual with 100% passion for passing on in an engaging and energetic way the essential skills required to be a successful Professional Coach. His delivery has such outstanding clarity that he makes the content of his training truly practical and memorable.

Howard Bryant

Managing Director of Retails Asia Limited | United Kingdom

I have a paradigm shift on what is truly transformative coaching compare with conventional coaching. This training offers me deep insights into the essence of powerful asking and active listening needed for effective coaching. What I really appreciate is the continual professional development and it clearly shows the commitment of the academy. 

Swandajani Gunadi

Director - Chief of Human Capital and Chief of Marketing for Adira Finance | Indonesia

Coach Masters Academy puts the "Masterful" into Masterful coaching and training. The Faculty Team knows how to bring the best out of people. Training with CMA has allowed me to surpass what I thought was possible and reach a level of understanding and confidence in my coaching skills beyond what I initially aimed for. But it was more than just an education, and it was "Life-Changing”.

CHARL SWART

MANAGING DIRECTOR I | South Africa

About the Main Facilitator

With nearly 20 years of experience as a Leadership Effectiveness and Transition Coach, Dr Ben Koh has brought the benefits of coaching to organizations helping leaders raise the bar on their performance and managing their success. He has been delivering C-Suite coaching services globally, for executives in leading corporations. Using his deep and evocative style of coaching, he enables leaders to experience powerful shift in their thinking and empowers them to lead from an inside-out approach. He partners with his clients and inspire them deeply to use their innate capacity to excel in what matters most to them and enabling to flourish in their full leadership capacity. He engages them in deep and focus learning conversation that stimulate them to reflect critically, align their personal and work values and hold themselves accountable to their decision.

title: Leadership Development Program | Executive Coaching Service
description: Get executive leadership coaching at Coach Masters Academy. Our executive coaching certification, leadership programs, & team coaching help leaders thrive.
h1: Executive Leadership Coaching Services for High‑Impact Leaders
content:
Unlock the full potential of your organization’s leaders with our executive coaching service. At Coach Master Academy, we provide executive coaching that helps high-potential talent enhance leadership performance, strategic thinking, and decision-making skills.

Our leadership development program guides internal leaders and organizations to drive measurable results and achieve long-term success. Register now to transform leadership potential into organizational results.

Empower Your Leaders with Executive Coaching that Drives Performance

Deliver Business Results Through Personalized Executive Coaching

McKinsey research indicates that 85% of companies with effective middle management experience higher performance metrics.

While senior leadership sets the direction and culture of an organization, leaders at every level contribute a huge part of its success. Team leaders, middle managers, and department heads interact with employees daily and directly shape the work environment, engagement, and satisfaction. These individuals are the conduits through which company values are translated into operational reality.

Our executive leadership coaching programs focus on developing the skills that matter most, helping your leaders guide their teams with confidence and clarity.

What is Executive Leadership Coaching?

Executive leadership coaching typically involves a series of one-on-one sessions between a coach and leaders across all levels of the organization. Coaches work closely with their clients to unlock potential, set clear goals, and develop tailored strategies to address real business challenges. Rather than following a standardized curriculum, executive coaching is highly personalized to meet each leader’s unique needs and context.

Many organizations now partner with external coaching services to deliver these sessions. While internal managers can effectively lead their teams, experienced executive coaches bring specialized expertise that accelerates leadership growth. In fact, Korn Ferry reports that one-third of Fortune 500 companies use external coaches as a standard part of their leadership development program for both executives and emerging leaders.

Research also highlights the strong value of executive leadership coaching. A study by MetrixGlobal LLC found that it delivers an average return on investment (ROI) of 788%, driven by improved productivity, stronger performance, and better employee retention.

Executive Coaching Program - Tailored for Leaders at All Levels

That Focuses on High-Impact Leadership Development

Our tailored leadership development program includes:

  • Senior Leadership Coaching: Strategic intervention for senior leaders navigating complex business challenges and driving transformation.
  • Mid-Level Manager Coaching: Strengthens communication, performance management, and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Team Coaching: This training program helps teams work more effectively together while supporting organizational goals.

Measurable Executive Coaching Impact & Organizational Outcomes

The success of our programs is measured through clearly defined key performance indicators (KPIs), goal achievement, and observable behavioral change. With a structured, evidence-based approach, we ensure our executive coaching service delivers tangible improvements in leadership effectiveness, productivity, and employee engagement.

Real-World Leadership Development for Everyday Challenges

Our coaching sessions emphasize practical application, equipping leaders to respond effectively to real-world challenges such as managing conflict and difficult conversations, improving team performance and accountability, and strengthening communication and stakeholder relationships.

Transformational Executive Coaching for Lasting Leadership Growth

Through guided reflection and targeted coaching, leaders develop deeper self-awareness, challenge existing assumptions, and redefine their leadership approach. This transformational process enables leaders to shift mindsets, adopt more effective leadership behaviors, and enhance decision-making and emotional intelligence.

Executive Leadership Coaching ROI - Measurable Business Impact

  • Improved management and leadership
  • Increased empowerment and ownership
  • Greater commitment and higher retention
  • Enhanced personal impact and performance
  • Accelerated personal development of high-potential individuals

Evidence-Based, Transformative Coaching Approach

We use the Awareness-Clarity-Choice (ACC) Conversation framework, which is an empirical approach that draws on multiple disciplines, including the latest research in positive psychology and adult learning development.

The ACC Conversation is delivered as a learning dialogue that evokes deeper awareness, clarity, and insight. Through intentional questioning and reflection, coaches help leaders surface their self-knowledge and bring it into conscious awareness, enabling them to use new understanding to create positive shifts in how they think, feel, and act. It allows them to reshape how they understand themselves, relate to others, and expand their sense of what is possible.

"With this emerging understanding, leaders can then tap into their potential and make empowering choices moving forward. These change experiences can trigger deep, fundamental revisions to beliefs, principles, and feelings, allowing people to modify their understanding of themselves and others."

Trusted Coaches with Proven Experience & Global Perspective

Is Your Best Guarantee for a Good Return on Investment.

Driven by our vision and our mastery of coaching, we partner with leaders to deliver sustainable, measurable results for their organizations.

With regional offices across Canada, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia and Oceania Pacific, we have the capacity and resources to deliver a top-tier global coaching program. Our global reach enables us to provide executive coaching services in multiple locations and languages, creating significant value for multinational organizations.

What sets us apart is the quality of our coaches. Our global team of executive coaches are graduates of our academy who have completed 145 hours of advanced coach training programs, ensuring leaders get consistent, high-quality coaching experience across all programs. They also have a combination of recognised coaching certifications, advanced academic degrees, and senior-level corporate backgrounds. 

Each coach has been chosen through a rigorous selection process so that they meet our high standards both in coaching practice and in business experience.

Customized Executive Coaching Engagements

Register Now

Coaching High-Potential Leaders and Emerging Executives

Through targeted coaching, these high-potential leaders and executives can build strategic thinking, influence, and executive presence, while strengthening emotional intelligence and stakeholder management. The program helps leaders bridge the gap between technical excellence and leadership impact, equipping them with the skills and confidence needed to step into bigger roles and deliver sustainable results.

Supporting Leadership Transitions & New Roles

We help leaders define new expectations, build credibility quickly, and adapt their leadership style to meet evolving demands. For leaders moving from technical roles to people leadership, the program focuses on strengthening communication, delegation, and team development skills. title: Expand Capacity for Deep Reflective Thinking-Coach Masters Academy
content:
Expand Capacity for Deep Reflective Thinking

Drawing on many years of fieldwork and research, Dr Ben Koh, the founder of Coach Masters Academy, has developed a proprietary transformative coaching framework known as the Awareness-Clarity-Choice (ACC) Conversation. It is an empirical approach that blends the science of Positive Psychology with the theories of transformative learning to support generative change. 

It is a dialogic conversation that seeks to heighten self-awareness and deepen the learning to draw out the emerging understanding.

The word “dialogic” refers to using a shared dialogue to explore the meaning of something.

The ACC Conversation uses an evocative inside-out approach to encourage people to reflect deeper in order to gain greater awareness, clarity, and understanding. This requires the coach to elicit and evoke people's self-knowledge, bringing it into their conscious awareness so they may use this understanding to create a fundamental shift in their thinking, feeling and actions. 

This is one of the distinct characteristics of the ACC Conversation - the spaciousness for people to sort through their thinking. The thought-provoking questioning process enables them to identify the issue at hand by addressing the dynamic gaps positively and constructively. This optimistic positivity would catapult them to a new understanding level and how they can experience their reality differently.

An inside-out approach to draw out insights

It provides the client with a safe space to explore his current reality objectively and gain a higher level of self-awareness which allows him to continually clarify and deepen his understanding of his being about the story he brings into the coaching space. Through the artful and masterful transformative coaching process, the client can emerge with new insights and learning that empowers him to tap into his strengths and take action to achieve the results that he truly desires.

Transformative coaching process requires the coach to have a high level of attention, awareness and openness to use oneself for the client's service. The coach needs to have the competencies to build rapport with the client, listens actively to the client’s story with non-judgmental compassion and at the same time curious about what is the shift that needs to happen in the broader system that the client is interacting with, what needs to shift in the relationship between the client and the issue he is describing, and for those shifts to occur, what needs to shift right now in the client.

While the coach is holding these questions in mind, he is comfortable with this tension without working out an answer intellectually, but waiting for a felt sense of what is necessary for the intended transformative purpose. The coach's understanding of the client’s situation starts with the broader view of the system he is part of and draws on his experience to stimulate the client to think, feel and explore new attitudes to identify the dynamic gap and create sustainable change. Coaching helps the client unearth and tap potential and creativity; co-ordinate career and personal life; increase the ability to cope with and welcome change; improve concentration, confidence, relaxation and decision-making; remove performance fears and anxieties, and eliminate unhealthy stress at work.

Experiencing a powerful shift in thinking

The transformative coaching approach enables sustainable change by creating a shift in the client’s mindset and emotional framing of their reality; rather than changing their choices within the current set of perceived possibilities which only addresses the situation and symptoms of client’s issues. The coaching process in this form of Coaching moves beyond new awareness and insight, to create a ‘felt shift’ in the space, where the client’s whole way of engaging with his issue has changed, including his verbal and non-verbal language. This newfound energy evokes commitment to action.

Effective personal development happens when one is increasingly clear about what they want, and more importantly, why they want what they want. The “hows” would naturally be developed once these “whats” and “whys” are clarified. The emphasis of defining one’s values and principles and aligning one’s behaviour and decisions based on this foundation would likely be one of the best coaching models to propel one to move forward in maximizing one’s potential when practised professionally. 

In conclusion, a transformational approach can create a more lasting impact than other methods for clients. This is consistent with the systemic perspective in that one part of the system fundamentally changes; the rest of the system will have to adapt to match it. This ultimately will facilitate client gaining a higher level of self-awareness that perpetuates personal effectiveness and development.

Drawing on many years of fieldwork and research, Dr Ben Koh, the founder of Coach Masters Academy, has developed a proprietary transformative coaching framework known as the Awareness-Clarity-Choice (ACC) Conversation. It is an empirical approach that blends the science of Positive Psychology with the theories of transformative learning to support generative change.

content:
FAQ

Here are some frequently asked questions. If your queries aren’t addressed here, we invite you to complete the Interest Form. Our dedicated Program Consultants are ready to provide personalised guidance and ensure you take the most suitable steps to enhance your learning journey.

Does the Coaching School offers a recognized certification?

There more than 67 certifying bodies for coaching but the “gold standard” is still International Coach Federation (ICF). Formed in 1995, today the ICF is the leading global organisation dedicated to advancing the coaching profession by setting high professional standards, providing independent certification, and building a network of credentialed coaches. If you plan to work mainly with corporate client, a recognized certificate may be required.

Why is coaching accreditation important? The coaching industry is at the verge of expanding with more and more people are hiring coaches to work with them on an ever-expanding range of issues. You can now find a coach for almost anything. This growth combined with an increasing public awareness of coaching has resulted in higher demands for accredited training and certified coaches. Clients want to know when they employ a coach that they are not just employing someone calling himself/ herself a coach, but that they have completed a rigorous training and accreditation process. The approval process involves a detailed analysis on the quality of the training, qualification and competencies of the trainers and the assessment process to ensure that the students enroll in the program are trained according to the standard of ICF core competencies.
What are the qualifications of the Master Trainer?

There are 2 important criteria to evaluate, (1) Training Certification and (2) Coaching Credential. The training certificate is a good indicator to assess the depth of knowledge while the coaching credential will inform the trainer’s real coaching experience. The trainer who is conducting the program must complete some level of coach training and be credentialed by ICF or another recognized body. If the coaching industry suffers from any setbacks, it is lack of coaching specific training prior to claiming the title of coach. Having good training competencies and sound knowledge are not enough, it must be coupled with rich experience in working with clients. The trainer must be an active practitioner so that he can demonstrate how the theory can be applied and integrated into real life application.

How importance is Certification and Credentialing?

Certification can shows that you have already completed the required training hours and have the sound knowledge and theory of practice but it does not necessarily guarantee that you have acquired the necessary skills to obtain the results. Participant applying for credential must complete the training hours and fulfill minimum client coaching hours. This is to ensure that the participants have real and substantial coaching experience. In non-licensed professions like coaching, credentialing is one surest way to ensure that the coach has acquired the knowledge and skill to deliver the results. Though certification and credential do not validate the proficiency and mastery of coaching, it can be a starting point for an international quality control standard and tangible criteria for client to choose their coach.

What are the Different types of ICF program Accreditation?

There are 3 types of ICF Program Accreditation:

  • Approved Coaching Specific Training Hours (ACSTH) with min. 60 hours coaching training
  • Approved Coaching Training Program (ACTP) with min. 125 hours coaching training
  • Continual Coaching Education (CCE)
What are the Different types of ICF Credentials?

There are 3 types of ICF Credentials:

  • Associate Certified Coach (ACC): An Associate Certified Coach is a coach who demonstrates a beginning level of knowledge and competence in their use of coaching skills and also demonstrates a basic knowledge of the difference between coaching and other professions in the way they use their coaching skills.
  • Professional Certified Coach (PCC): A Professional Certified Coach is a coach who demonstrates a clear knowledge of coaching skills, but is still somewhat dependent on tools from their coach training and still learning how to fully partner with the client and put all of the tools together in a way that serves the client powerfully. A PCC also demonstrates a firm knowledge of the difference between coaching and other professions in the way they use their coaching skills.
  • Master Certified Coach (MCC): A Master Certified Coach is a coach who demonstrates a fluent and easy use of coaching skills in a way that powerfully partners with the client and serves the client exploration and learning. A MCC also demonstrates a clear and deep knowledge of the difference between coaching and other professions in the way they use their coaching skills.
ICF Credentialing Program: Why was it Developed?

In the early days, coaches shared two things: a passionate interest in coaching and for making a difference in the world through the “tool” of coaching. There was no particular “definition” of coaching and no particular guidelines or standards by which to judge the efficacy of coaching. As the ICF began to grow, it became apparent that the association needed to explore more fully what coaching is in such a way as to inform the consumer and clarify the integrity of the evolving profession. The association needed to be able to clearly evaluate the competency of a coach “in action,” as well as define the training standards that would get them to the level of competency.

How were the ICF Coaching Core Competencies Developed?

In 1998, various ICF committees were formed to address the development of standards, ethics, definition of coaching, and more. Hence, the ICF Portfolio Exam committee was created. At that time, they were faced with 2 pressing issues:

1) ICF needed to agree upon and finalize strong and clearly articulated competencies, and, 2) ICF needed to be clear that the competencies that were created truly represented coaching.

The Committee invited the heads of all of the existing coach training schools (eight visible at the time), to participate in this project. These schools were: Hudson Institute, Newfield, Coaches Training Institute, Coach U, Coach for Life, Success Unlimited Network, Academy of Coach Training and New Ventures West. For the next year (1999), they came together and through their various theoretical bases of coaching, they had co-created and finally all agreed on, the competencies that are the core of coaching as we know it today. It was the first big step in the growth of coaching.

title: Have the Courage to Ask-Coach Masters Academy
content:
By: Marshall Goldsmith (To be published by the Leader to Leader Institute, 2005)

Peter Drucker has a great way with words. He distills meaningful concepts into short phrases more effectively than anyone I have ever met. I have had the privilege of being on the Board of the Drucker Foundation (and now the Leader to Leader Institute) for many years. At one of our early Drucker Foundation Board meetings, Peter observed,

The leader of the past knew how to tell, the leader of the future will know how to ask.

Why is asking so important?  Almost all of the leaders that I meet manage knowledge workers.  Peter has defined knowledge workers as people who know more about what they are doing than their boss does.  It is hard to tell people what to do and how to do it – when they already know more than we do!  In today’s rapidly changing world, we need to ask, listen and learn from everyone around us.  As Peter recently stated “Leaders need to be willing to start with asking the question,

‘What needs to be done?’

Asking works!  This isn’t just a theory – as research shows – it is a fact.  My partner, Howard Morgan and I recently published a study on leadership development programs involving over 11 thousand leaders and 86 thousand of their co-workers from eight major corporations

[1].  Our findings were very clear.  Leaders that ask co-workers to provide suggestions for improvement, listen to their co-workers, learn from the people around them and consistently follow-up are seen as becoming more effective.  Leaders that don’t ask – don’t get much better.  A few years ago, Leader to Leader published a similar study with relationship customers

[2] and found very similar results.  External customer satisfaction goes up when customer service representatives ask, listen, learn and follow-up.

In addition to being supported by research, asking just makes common sense.  When people ask us for our input, listen to us, try to learn from us and follow-up to see if they are getting better – our relationship with them almost invariably improves.

I have only one question.  Why don’t we do it?

One of the major reasons that we don’t ask is our inflated ego.  When I have asked over 50,000 leaders to “rate themselves” relative to their professional peers – the results are very consistent – and very amazing!  About 60% of all leaders rank themselves in the “top 10%” of their professional peer group, almost 85% say they are in the “top 20%” and over 98% claim to be in the “top half”!  The performance of the company has very little to do with the self-assessment of its leaders.  I have done this exercise with leaders in four companies that were considered (at that time) as the “most admired” in America – the results were about the same.  I have also done this exercise with leaders in two companies that were facing bankruptcy – the results were almost identical!

When we become successful we are often delusional about the reasons for our success.  Successful people tend to attribute good results to our own motivation and ability.  We tend to attribute poor results to environmental factors, bad luck or random chance. When we over-rate our own performance and knowledge, we can easily justify not asking others for their input.  After all, why should we ask others, when in our own mind we already know more than they do!

Although inflated ego is one important reason that we don’t ask, it is not the biggest reason – the biggest reason is fear.

Recently I asked the VP of Customer Satisfaction in a major organization, “Should your employees be asking their key customers for feedback – listening – learning and following-up to ensure service keeps getting better?”

“Of course!” he exclaimed.

“How important it this to your company?” I inquired – egging him on to be more enthusiastic.  “It’s damn important!” he cried out.

I then lowered my voice and asked, “Have you ever asked your wife for feedback on how you can become a better husband?” He stopped, thought for a second, and sighed “No.”

My interrogation continued, “Who is more important – your company’s customers or your wife?” “My wife – of course!” he sadly noted.

“If you believe in asking so much, why don’t you do it at home?”  I inquired.  He ruefully admitted, “Because I am afraid of the answer.”

Why don’t most of us ask – even though we know we should?  We don’t ask because – deep down inside – we are afraid of the answers.

My suggestions are very simple:

As a leader get in the habit of asking key co-workers for their ideas on “What needs to be done?”  Thank them for their input, listen to them, learn as much as you can, incorporate the ideas that make the most sense and follow-up to ensure that real, positive change is occurring.

As a coach – encourage the people that you are coaching to ask, listen and learn from everyone around them.  Be a great role model for learning – then ask the people you are coaching to learn in the same way that you are.  As an executive coach, I find that my clients can learn a lot more from their key stakeholders than they ever learn from me!

As a friend and family member – ask the people that you love how you can be a better partner, friend, parent or child.  Listen to their ideas.  Don’t get so busy with work that you forget that they may well be the most important people in your life.

Improving interpersonal relationships doesn’t have to take a lot of our time.  It does require having the courage to ask for important people’s opinions and the discipline to follow-up and do something about what we learn.

[1] “Leadership is a Contact Sport” strategy+business, Fall 2004
[2] “Increasing Customer Satisfaction”, M. Goldsmith, H. Morgan and A. Freas, Leader to Leader, Winter 1997

Foundational Advantage: Certification Starter Track

Everyone can support someone in a conversation.

Not every conversation can create real change.

A coaching conversation is more than asking good questions; it can become a powerful catalyst for transformative change. Many approaches struggle to create lasting impact because they lose sight of coaching’s fundamental purpose: enabling meaningful change in how people see and respond to what they are facing.

Foundational Advantage is where you begin. You learn a clear, practical way of coaching people that helps them see their situation differently and move towards meaningful change — at work, at home, and in everyday life.

The application is versatile and can be used in various contexts.

  • Support people in making better decisions when they face dilemmas
  • Help them figure out a way forward when they feel stuck
  • Enable greater clarity and understanding when they are sorting through confusion or frustration.

Program Snapshot

Who it's for: People new to coaching, or leaders who want stronger coaching skills in their role Time commitment: About 70 learning hours over approximately 16 weeks. Certification Pathway: This program provides the ICF Level 1 education required to apply for the ACC credential.

Program Structure

  • Learning Lab :12 Sessions
  • Practical Lab :12 Sessions
  • Enrichment Lab :3 Sessions
  • Mentoring Lab :3 Sessions
  • Engagement Lab :2 Sessions

Program Description

Learning Lab: Understanding What You Are Working With

You begin by unpacking the science behind real change, so your coaching is grounded in more than tips and techniques. You gain a clearer view of what drives people’s responses and why some conversations open new possibilities while others keep people in the same place. Starting here sharpens everything you learn next.

Module A: Understand What Makes Coaching Transformational

You experience coaching as a different kind of conversation — one designed to shift how people see and respond. You explore what makes a coaching partnership work, how patterns of thinking show up in what people say and do, and how reflective dialogue helps them put words to what they have been feeling but could not yet express.

 Key Insights You Will Explore

  • What sets coaching apart from advising, helping, or mentoring
  • How thinking patterns shape the flow and tone of a conversation
  • How reflective dialogue brings out what people really mean
Module B: Seeing the Story Behind the Story

Here, your skill development begins. Using our proprietary narrative analysis, you learn to notice what a person highlights and how their story reveals what truly matters to them. This gives you a clearer way to support someone when they need to step back, see differently, or consider new possibilities.

 Key Insights You Will Explore

  • Listening for and capturing the essence of what someone is saying
  • Noticing how “gain” and “loss” perspectives shape their focus
  • Seeing how their way of thinking limits what feels possible
  • Using personal stories to recognise what holds meaning for them
Module C: Coaching with the ACC Conversation

Here you bring everything together. You work with our proprietary Awareness–Clarity–Choice (ACC) Conversation — a simple, proven, science-based coaching process that helps people slow down their thinking, see their situation more clearly, and recognise what is really influencing their reactions.

 Key Insights You Will Explore

  • How to guide a person through the ACC Conversation in real time
  • How to stay with their meaning instead of rushing to action or advice
  • How clearer focus and understanding support more grounded decisions
Practical Lab & Enrichment Lab: Learning by Doing & Observing

This is where you build the confidence to use and adapt it in your real-life context.

 Practical Lab: Applying the Approach in Real Conversations

In the Practical Lab, you put the approach into practice through real conversations and structured case studies. You see how the method actually unfolds in practice, build confidence using it in your own context, and receive guidance from an experienced coach supervisor. This helps you link the concepts to live coaching moments and notice the subtleties in coach–client interactions.

 Enrichment Lab: Witnessing Mastery in Action

In the Enrichment Lab, you have the rare opportunity to watch mastery in action. You observe the same approach applied at a highly skilled level in a real conversation, with space to reflect on what you are seeing. This gives you a clear picture of how the method works when executed well, and a concrete sense of what to aim for as your own practice grows.

Mentoring Lab: Seeing What You Couldn’t See Alone

In the Mentoring Lab, you receive focused feedback on your coaching conversations. Your mentor helps you notice what you did well, what you missed, and how your way of thinking shapes your questions and responses. This kind of guided reflection strengthens your awareness and supports progress that is hard to achieve on your own.

Engagement Lab: Designing & Managing the Coaching Journey

You learn to hold coaching as a series of connected conversations rather than isolated sessions. You design how an engagement begins, how each conversation builds on the last, and how it concludes with clarity. You work with simple structures that help leaders, internal coaches, and practitioners start, sustain, and grow a coaching practice with confidence.

title: Leading by Listening-Coach Masters Academy
content:
The old paradigm that the leaders are supposed to tell their followers what and how to do things, is losing its plot in the modern era. The new leader understands that he has to harness the power and potential of the people and this is done by listening to them. Listening is an art which needs to be learnt and practised It is perhaps the most essential skill for a modern leader.

Listening is much much more than hearing. Listening involves getting into the shoes of the other person. It involves empathy and an understanding of emotions.

Data from exit interviews across the industries and cultures shows that employees are disgruntled because they don’t feel engaged. Engaging employees is not just top down one-way communication. Engagement involves listening. When the employees feel being listened to, they feel engaged. Many managers feel afraid that if they let their employees express too much they will become too demanding and eventually dissatisfied because managers would not be able to meet those demands. Listening is not about agreeing – it is about understanding. Only when you understand the other side completely, you will be able to enter into a conclusive dialogue and be able to influence. You can be a good listener and also assertive at the same time.

Listening is a key coaching skill and the leaders who use coaching as their conversation style, use it successfully to motivate and influence their people and stakeholders.

title: Mastering Mindfulness in Coaching-Coach Masters Academy
content:
As a lifetime Social Worker, who also experienced living in a contemplative convent for over two years, I was intrigued by how I could bring this two world together. So I dedicated my career to training as a Certified Coach with the International Coach Federation and also became an active Mindfulness Practitioner. In reality, how can these two practices co-exist? In theory and practice, let us explore the impact that Coaching and mindfulness could have on coachees experience and more fundamentally on one's coaching style. 

The ICF core competencies guides and trains coaches in developing the skills of active listening, creating awareness and establishing trust with the client. While Mindfulness Practitioners are trained in improving their mental faculties of attention, intention and reflection, to bring non-judgemental attention to their daily experiences, as mindfulness master Jon Kabat Zinn explains, "mindfulness is the moment to moment, non-judgmental awareness." 

With this understanding, how can mindfulness complement both the coach and the coachee? Director of the Global Coaching Practice at the Centre for Creative Leadership, Douglas Riddle states that "mindful coaches perfect a form of conscious and comfortable simultaneous attention to themselves, their coachee, the relationship between them, and the mental, emotional, and relational dynamics occurring at the moment."

To highlight the impact of mindfulness for the coach and coachee, the author of Mindful Coaching, Liz Hall, conducted an online international survey of over 150 coaches from regions including the UK and the US. The survey revealed the top reasons why coaches practice mindfulness: to help them live more at the moment (74%), be more self-aware (73%), manage/prevent stress (67%), and be more present for their coachees (65%). And the main reasons they use mindfulness explicitly with coachees: to help the coachees become more self-aware (70%), be calmer/less anxious (59%), better manage stress/be more centred (55%) and better manage reactions/responses (51%).

When working in partnership with coachees who are experiencing the inability to relax, have low self-esteem, or are working through stressful situations, the benefits of mindfulness can shift each of these areas. The proven benefits of mindfulness have been to increase an individual's ability to relax, to develop higher self-esteem and to work through stressful life situations positively. Mindfulness is a practice of exploring how to consciously and systematically work with stress and the challenges and demands of everyday life by not turning away from them, but learning to be resilient with and through these challenges. Coachees often find that space to think, feel and explore while staying invigorated within the relationship. Besides, this dynamic has the potential to create genuine collaboration between coach and coachee. 

Modern brain research has shown that we move in and out of various states of focused or unfocused attention throughout our day. Coaching allows someone to stay on a line of thought until it yields new perspectives and answers. It proves powerful, especially when these are questions that might have hindered us for a long time. The coach wants to create an encounter in which the two people are in synchronized attention, where vast amounts of mental and emotional energy can be directed at the development of the coachee. This is a kind of mutual trance state, along the lines of being "in the zone" in sports, and most people have experienced it only briefly. The mindful coach can elicit this state and maintain it for the growth of the coachee.

The value of a meditative practice within Coaching is a way to master one's mind, to silence the ramblings of our everyday life and agenda. This approach can train the coach as they journey into a vast mental and emotional journey with their coachees. Coaches are committed to co-creating a relationship with the coachees, to be mindful in listening to the coachee's concerns, goals, values and beliefs. Mindful coaches provide coachees with the space to wander from viewpoint to viewpoint, from one incomplete thought to another until they begin to become aware of the whole idea and the basis for clarity. Entering the coaching conversation with a "still mind" is key to letting something happen in someone else. For all conversations, when someone hears us with an open, still mind, we have the space to sense our worth and value. This is the essence of Coaching.

Mindful Coaching is continuing to make its mark in the coaching world. With society having an ever-increasing demand on our time and energy, taking a few moments in our day to be centred and to centre our coachees has rich benefits in gaining clarity, finding solutions, managing stress and living with more depth. 

By: Renee Hodgkinston, ICF ACC Credential Coach and CMA Program Director for Beijing. 

Renee explores how coaching and mindfulness can co-exist in theory and in practice and explores the impact it has on clients and coaches' coaching style.

Mastery Advantage: MCC Track Enabling Developmental Change in Your Coaching Conversation

Where MCC mastery and developmental coaching become one coherent practice.

You already have serious training.
Now you want a way of coaching that can hold developmental change at an MCC standard.

Mastery Advantage is the 3rd level of the Transformative Edge™. It is designed for experienced coaches, typically PCC or equivalent, who want their next phase of growth to be both MCC credential-ready and developmentally grounded.

This programme is your Level 3 Pathway and practical preparation for the MCC Performance Evaluation. At the same time, it deepens your use of our proprietary transformational approach so you can work consistently at the level of meaning-making and perspective, not only at the level of issues and goals.

Since its launch in 2020, Mastery Advantage has supported 64 Coach Practitioners on their MCC journey, with many passing their performance evaluation on the first submission.

Program Snapshot

Who it's for: Experienced coaches and practitioners, typically at PCC level or equivalent, who want to specialise in developmental coaching and prepare seriously for MCC.

Time commitment: About 80 learning hours over approximately 24 weeks. Offered once a year as a single global cohort, supporting depth of supervision, continuity, and a focused learning community.

Certification Pathway: Provides ICF Level 3–accredited education and mentoring, meeting the Level 3 training requirement and serving as core preparation for the MCC Performance Evaluation.

Program Structure

  • Learning Lab :5 Sessions
  • Competency Lab :12 Sessions
  • Practical Lab :12 Sessions
  • Enrichment Lab :3 Sessions
  • Mentoring Lab :3 Sessions

The Two Promises of Mastery Advantage

Mastery Advantage is one of the few Level 3 journeys that deliberately ties your MCC preparation to your growth as a developmental coach. In the same conversations and recordings, you build a body of work that both meets the credentialing standard and reflects how you truly want to coach.

The result is clear: you are positioned to apply for MCC with confidence while standing in a strong professional identity as a masterful practitioner of transformational, developmental coaching. This dual focus comes to life in two promises:

Coaching that clearly demonstrates MCC-level Mastery

You develop your practice so the ICF Core Competencies and Level 3 markers show up as a natural expression of how you think, listen, and respond in the moment.

 You will:

  • Have a clear understanding of what MCC-consistent coaching looks and sounds like in real conversations.
  • Practise at this level repeatedly, with structured feedback that connects your moves to the markers.
  • Learn to hear your own recordings differently - recognising where you are operating at MCC level and where your coaching drops below, and knowing what to adjust in the next minute, not only in the next session.
A distinctive mastery in coaching for developmental change

You deepen your capacity to coach developmental and intentional change as your primary field of practice.

 You will:

  • Work at the level of how clients make sense of their world - the structures of meaning that sit behind many presenting challenges.
  • Spot recurring patterns of interpretation across situations and sessions, and engage with them in a grounded, respectful way.
  • Support clients to grow into more capable perspectives that can hold greater complexity and sustain different choices.
What You Walk Away With

By the end of Mastery Advantage, you will be able to:

  • Hold developmental conversations at MCC standard - spacious, precise, client-led, and grounded in clear intent.
  • Work with the structure of meaning-making - noticing how a client's perspective is organised and choosing interventions from that awareness.
  • Shape coaching as a developmental journey - where each session connects to a coherent growth trajectory, not a series of disconnected topics.
  • Invite learning beyond the session - supporting clients to test new ways of seeing and acting in the situations that matter most.
  • Prepare and select recordings for your MCC Performance Evaluation, with clarity on what to submit, how to refine them, and how to learn from feedback.

In your recordings, this will show up as:

  • More spacious, client-led conversations with fewer but more impactful interventions.
  • Clearer alignment between what the client wants and where you keep the focus throughout the session.
  • Stronger evidence of partnering - less steering, more co-creating, and deeper trust in the client's resourcefulness.

Your practice becomes a reliable vehicle for developmental change, and you stand on a solid foundation for your MCC application

Why Mastery Advantage

MCC Results You Can Trust

Built from years of mentoring coaches into MCC, this programme gives you a tested, proven pathway with practical, concrete support at every step. You receive:

  • A 50-page MCC marker guide that turns abstract standards into a precise reference as you prepare your recordings.
  • Access to a curated library of ICF-approved MCC-level coaching conversations you can study, analyse, and use to benchmark your own work.
  • Developmental feedback from experienced MCC faculty who understand both the spirit and the standards of MCC-level practice.

You are not navigating Level 3 and MCC preparation alone or in the dark. You are accompanied by a global team that has walked this path with many coaches before you.

Powered by the Transformative Edge™ approach

Mastery Advantage builds on CMA's proprietary transformational framework used across Foundational and Competency Advantage. At this level, you refine the same approach into an MCC-consistent way of thinking and responding, rather than collecting new tools.

Your developmental thinking and your MCC preparation grow together. Every element of the programme is designed so that what strengthens your coaching for change also strengthens your MCC readiness - in the same conversations and the same recordings.

How Does The Learning Work

How Does The Learning Work

You work from a clear map of intentional and developmental change, linked directly to how you hold conversations.

  • You practice live in focused Labs with peers and with supervision, so insights move quickly into observable skills in your recordings.
  • You observe masterful coaching at this level and debrief what you see, so “MCC-level coaching” becomes concrete and recognisable rather than abstract.
  • You receive tailored mentoring through your own recorded sessions, explicitly mapped to Level 3 and MCC expectations.

The design gives you repeated cycles of SEE -> PRACTICE -> OBSERVE -> RECEIVE FEEDBACK -> REFINE, so your growth is steady and visible in your actual coaching.

Your Next Step

Mastery Advantage is designed as an intensive, high-touch Level 3 journey. To protect the depth of supervision and peer learning, each global cohort is limited to 15 participants on a first-come, first-served basis. A brief interview is required to assess readiness and mutual fit, so the cohort environment supports everyone’s development.

The detailed structure, dates, completion requirements, and investment options are available in the Mastery Advantage brochure.

If you are ready to bring MCC competency mastery and mastery of coaching for change together:

  • Download the brochure for the full programme outline.
  • Submit your expression of interest, and we will arrange a short conversation to explore readiness, timing, and fit for the next global cohort.

Mastery Advantage is where you prepare for MCC and deepen your practice as a transformational, developmental coach – in one coherent, thoughtfully designed journey shared with a small group of equally committed practitioners.

This module will cover the transformative principles required to create a powerful perspective transformation.

    The Power of Inquiry I The Power of Observation I Structural Layout of the Thought-Process I 7 Elements of the Story

The coaching process stimulates reflective thinking resulting in a powerful shift in thinking to align their greatest inspiration with action and hold them accountable for their decision. It is a deep and focused coaching conversation that shifts the attention from a situational context to personal awareness, thus uncovering how people construct their mewling, understanding what matters most, and then using this emerging understanding to create a clear path forward.
