h1: Become an ICF-Certified Coach with Coach Masters Academy
content:
Entering the field of professional coaching is more than a vocational pivot; it is a rigorous commitment to the evolution of your own potential and leadership presence. At Coach Masters Academy, we provide a transformational pathway to helping you achieve your coaching certification through a proprietary framework that transcends conventional methodology.

ICF Coaching Education that Starts Where Real Change Begins

Not just coaching skills, but a science-based way of working with real change.

True mastery requires a science-based methodology to facilitate genuine and lasting transformation. At Coach Masters Academy, our ICF coaching certification pathway is built upon a decade of research into how human change actually occurs. This framework allows you to move beyond surface-level fixes to address the core of how people live, lead, and relate to one another.

As coaching matures into a high-stakes global discipline, the calibre of your training is an essential market differentiator. We provide an ICF-accredited training program that aligns with global standards while equipping you with the skills to navigate complex human dynamics.

By choosing a scientifically backed education, you learn a reliable way to navigate complex conversations that shape lives and systems.

Globally Recognized, Science-Based, and Aligned with ICF Coaching Certification

As a global coaching school, Coach Masters Academy offers a comprehensive suite of ICF certification programs for those seeking the highest level of professional excellence. Our curriculum is built on rigorous, science-based principles and is aligned with the International Coaching Federation’s core competencies.

As one of the few institutions worldwide approved to deliver an ICF-accredited training program across the full continuum of mastery, we support you through every stage of your development. Our framework, The Transformative Edge™, provides a unified approach to understanding how people think and decide. By enrolling in our certification pathway, you join an elite faculty and a global community or professional coaches.

Build a Credible Coaching Practice that Drives Real Change in Everyday Conversations

Since 2011, practitioners and leaders in many countries have used this ICF-accredited coaching training program to work with meaningful change in everyday conversations about work, relationships, life transitions, and the choices that shape how people live and lead. Whether you’re pursuing professional coaching certification or bringing this into your leadership, you are building your practice with an established, credible coaching training provider recognized across the coaching industry.

Proven Success: Coaching Cohorts, Graduates, and More

452

Cohort Delivered from 2012 to 2024

7240

Graduates Completed the training

Your Pathway to ICF Certification and Coaching Success

ICF Credential Paths: From ACC to MCC

At Coach Masters Academy, we understand that people come to coaching from different places, which is why our ICF coaching certification programs are organized into different stages. Our flagship Transformative Edge™ framework provides the intellectual scaffolding required to navigate these levels of expertise:

  • Associate Certified Coach (ACC): This entry-level credential focuses on foundational skills and the practical application of the core coaching competencies.
  • Professional Certified Coach (PCC): This mid-level path is for practitioners who demonstrate consistent proficiency and a deeper understanding of the coaching relationship.
  • Master Certified Coach (MCC): This represents the highest level of mastery, signifying a coach who has reached the pinnacle of expertise and intuitive practice.
Foundational Advantage: Building the Coaching Mindset

With our ICF coaching certification program, you can move beyond surface fixes and quick questions toward core competencies such as ethical practice, active listening, and targeted questioning.

You learn to coach at the level where meaning guides action, not just at the level of problems and solutions.

Competency Advantage: Coaching Skill set that Engages the Whole Person

Our ICF-certified coaching programs emphasize competency-based learning to help you engage the whole person. With practical coaching exercises and live practice opportunities, you learn to work with the whole meaning system, so your coaching touches the person behind the performance, not only the role they are in.

Mastery Advantage: Enabling Developmental Change

The coaching training is designed for the MCC level of coaching. You will move beyond session-by-session fixes to intentional developmental growth. This mastery prepares you to address deep-seated patterns, improving your practice to the highest professional standards of the coaching industry.

Collective Advantage: Coaching the Team to Learn and Think Together

With these ICF coaching certification programs that focuses on team coaching, you can unlock shared meaning and prepare for the growing field of collective intelligence. You learn to work at the level where a team's shared meaning is created, so you can coach the way they are thinking together, not just the agenda in front of them.

Explore Your Coaching Pathway: Foundational to Mastery

Let's map the coaching journey that fits where you are now.

Our ICF coaching certification programs provide clear pathways from ACC to MCC. In our leadership coaching programs, we can also help you align your goals with the rigorous standards required for global mastery.

Certification Starter Track

Advanced Competency Certification Bridging Foundational to Mastery

Prepare for your journey toward the Professional Certified Coach level through our rigorous ICF coaching program. This track focuses on advanced coaching skills that move conversations from simple solutions to psychological shifts. Our ICF-accredited coach training program teaches you to coach at the level where meaning guides action, not just at the level of problems and solutions.

Professional Certification Track: Preparing for ICF Credentials

Advanced Competency Certification Bridging Foundational to Mastery

Elevate your practice with an ICF-accredited training program that prepares you for the Professional Certified Coach credential. This coaching program develops the advanced skills needed to hold the whole meaning system of your client. You will learn to touch the person behind the performance, addressing the values and concerns that shape their reality.

MCC Track: Master Your Coaching Skills to Lead at the Highest Level

Mastery Advantage Becoming a Leader in Coaching

Our MCC leadership training program is designed for when you want to work at the level where life patterns are formed, moving beyond session-by-session fixes. The step up in your ICF coaching certification journey, this program focuses on advanced leadership coaching and personal mastery. At the same time, it helps you see how a person grows and responds to their professional environment.

Team Coaching Certification Track: Leading Teams to Success

Collective Advantage Coaching Teams and Groups to Achieve Real Change

This ICF-certified coaching program is ideal when groups keep circling the same problems, and you want to help them think together in a way that actually moves them forward.

Unlike standard coaching programs, this track focuses on the level where a team’s shared meaning is created. You learn to work at the level where a team's shared meaning is created, so you can coach the way they are thinking together, not just the agenda in front of them.

ICF Coaching Education with the Transformative EdgeTM

How Your Coaching Professional Pathway Is Structured

The Transformative Edge™ pathway is built in clear stages called Advantages. Each Advantage adds a new layer to your practice and connects to a specific point on the ICF credential roadmap. You can see where you are starting, what comes next, and how each step supports your path toward ACC, PCC, or MCC.

Across every Advantage, you are working with one coherent way of thinking about change. The same core framework runs through your learning from the first conversation you practise to the most complex work you take on. What shifts at each stage is the depth of work you can hold and the kind of conversations you are ready to lead.

Choosing Your Intake

Wherever you are in the world, you can begin when you are ready.
Our global cohorts run year-round, so you can join an intake that fits your time zone, schedule, and learning rhythm.
Explore upcoming dates at: https://www.coachmastersacademy.com/events/calendar

If you are new to coaching

For those who are beginning their coaching journey or bringing coaching into their leadership, the pathway offers two main routes:

Certification Starter Track - Foundational Advantage
  • Your starting point for transformational coaching education.
  • It builds your coaching mindset and core method and meets the education requirement for the ACC credential through an ICF Level 1 pathway.
Professional Certification Track - [ Foundational + Competency Advantage ]
  • A continuous journey for those who want to coach at a professional standard.
  • It deepens your practice against ICF competency markers and fulfils the education requirement for the PCC credential through an ICF Level 2 pathway.
Exploratory Track - 14 Learning Sessions Only

Perhaps you are intrigued by what this program offers but have no intention, at least for now, of pursuing a professional coaching certification.

If that is where you are, we have good news: the Exploratory Track allows you to complete the Learning Lab from the Foundational Advantage as a stand-alone experience.

It is for people who want to understand how change works and apply it in their own life and work, with the option to continue into the certification pathway later.

If you are an experienced coach practitioner

For practitioners who already have coach training or an ICF credential, the pathway offers routes that build on what you have:

Credit Transfer Track - Competency Advantage
  • For practitioners who already hold accredited Level 1 or ACSTH training.
  • This option recognises your prior learning and supports you in completing the Competency Advantage, aligning you with an ICF Level 2 pathway and preparing you for a PCC application.
Collective Advantage - Team Coaching Track
  • For practitioners who have completed at least 70 hours of coaching training and want to extend their practice into team coaching.
  • This track focuses on coaching teams to think and work together, so you can support leadership teams and groups where collective insight and alignment matter.
Mastery Advantage - MCC Track
  • For experienced coach practitioners who already hold a PCC credential and are ready to refine their practice toward mastery.
  • This program prepares you to work at a developmental level and to meet MCC-level performance evaluation requirements within an ICF Level 3 pathway.

Six regional offices. One Transformative EdgeTM pathway.

Wherever you are based, you can engage with the same Transformative Edgeâ„¢ approach and be supported by a team in your region who understands your context.

  • Global standard - you learn within a proven Transformative Edgeâ„¢ framework applied across multiple regions and cultures.
  • Regional presence - local teams support your intake, schedule, and fees in line with your time zone and market.
  • Human support - you can speak directly with someone responsible for guiding your learning journey and pathway.

A short conversation with your regional office can help you sort through options, understand fees and timing, and see whether this pathway fits your season and goals. Use the contact details below to connect with the team closest to you and take the next step that makes sense for you now.

Toward Mastery - Mentor Coaching with Dr Ben Koh

Coaches change lives by empowering individuals to go after what they most desire and achieve a satisfaction they never thought possible.

The Mentor Coaching program has been developed specifically for Coaches who want to change lives. You will be well on your way to mastering the ICF Core Coaching Competencies following your Coach Masters Academy transformative coach training. Now, with practice and Dr Ben's guidance, you will have expert help to master the coaching process and accelerate your learning.

Ben is a true master of his craft. He is authentic, energetic and engaging. He was personally mentored by ICF pioneers such as Janet Harvey, Amorah Ross, Jenny Bird, Molly Gordon, and Duncan Coppock. Since then, he has trained and supported more than 2000 coaches across the globe in their professional development from 2013 to 2023

Ben knows how to help you take your coaching to the next level. His gentle approach will leave you with insights that will help you recognise and appreciate your strengths, and together, you will uncover your hidden potential for greater effectiveness and artistry.

You will return your renewed confidence to your client sessions with even better results.

How the mentor coaching works?

As a Certified Mentor Coach, Ben will review your coaching conversations with real clients. His focus will be on assessing your skills in relation to the process and flow of the conversation. The objective of mentor coaching is for you to hone your coaching awareness skills.

Ben will analyse your client's responses based on your questions and then look behind the conversation to help you discover your thought processes and enable you to fully demonstrate the competencies at the credential level qualification you are seeking. Through this process, you deepen your learning of yourself which helps you to better observe your inner processes in relation to how you help your clients as i.e. What is happening within you and what happened and why it matters. In a supportive and affirmative manner, you are then offered valuable suggestions on where your growth opportunities are

The Mentor Coaching Package will include

  •         Review of your recording
  •         Prepare Process Review Report
  •         Debrief to identify growth opportunities

  • Competency Review: Based on the ICF Assessor System, this review will provide you with an in-depth review of the demonstration of the Core Competencies in your coaching session. You will receive valuable feedback with practical solutions on how best you can improve to meet the credential requirements you are applying for.

Process Review: Your recordings are analysed segment by segment. You will receive valuable detailed feedback about improving the coaching process to demonstrate mastery in coaching the client for awareness. Although labour-intensive, this process enables Ben to provide practical suggestions, including actual questions you can use, that will allow you to improve your coaching process.

The Review Report and Ben's feedback will be provided from your transcript recordings. This report will suggest how you can improve the flow of the conversation to allow the client to go deeper and learn more.

Sample example of feedback report

Here are some samples of the reports you can expect to receive from the mentor coaching:

Mentor coaching package

Your mentoring sessions will focus on correcting, improving and enhancing your ability to demonstrate the core competencies to meet the specific level you are applying for. Depending on your competencies, you can opt for the following Package:

Package 1 [ Standard Package ] @ US$1200

This package is designed for those who wish to apply for your ICF Credential at ACC

This extensive package is designed especially for those applying for ICF credentials at MCC. It is also beneficial for those who wish to continue to hone their coaching skills to heighten their awareness and deepen their understanding of mastery skills. From 2019 to 2024, Dr Ben supported 50 coaches in achieving the MCC Credential.

content:
Dr. Ben Koh's - Founder

co founder

Dr. Ben Koh's

Unassuming Beginning with a Noble Mission

Dr. Ben Koh's pioneering spirit and strong belief in transformational coaching established our foundation in 2010 within the education sector of Kazakhstan. Today, we are a leading global coaching academy. We take pride in our rich legacy, which spans a decade of milestones, including our notable rebranding to align with our international goals. We want our story to inform and inspire you to embark on this coaching educational journey with us.

  • The Visionary Inception

    It all started in Kazakhstan in 2009 when Dr Ben had the opportunity to introduce coaching into the education sector. This initiative aimed to equip teachers with the necessary coaching skills to facilitate students’ personal growth and leadership. This ambitious and inspiring vision truly made a difference, leading to the establishment of the "I Am Life Coach" Academy to achieve this goal.

    2009 - 2011

  • Rebranding

    The pivotal moment came when the program was introduced to surrounding countries and received overwhelming success. With growing pride and humble hearts, we rebranded to Coach Masters Academy in 2012, reflecting our commitment to global reach. This was not just a simple name change. It is a bold statement of our commitment to pioneering a science-based approach. We embraced this new epoch with open arms.

    2012

  • Global Office established in Singapore, and Southeast Asian expansion.

    When Dr. Ben was relocated to Singapore, he established the Global Office there and began expanding into neighbouring countries. In a short time, he set up local offices in Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, and the Philippines to support our growth in Southeast Asia. This initiative marked a significant milestone for CMA as we confidently established our presence in the region.

    2013 - 2014

  • Expansion to the South Asia and Oceania Pacific Region

    CMA has rapidly risen to become one of the foremost academies in Southeast Asia. With this strong momentum, we are confidently expanding into South Asia and the Oceania Pacific region and establishing local offices in India, Sri Lanka, Hong Kong, and New Zealand.

    2015 - 2017

  • Marked our Expansion to the Middle East & Gulf

    Building on our success in Asia, Dr Ben initiated global expansion, starting with the UAE in 2017. In 2018, CMA became the first academy to enter Lebanon, establishing a local office there. In the later year, CMA played a crucial role in creating the ICF Beirut Chapter. In 2019, we introduced the first Arabic version of our program and expanded into Saudi Arabia. We established local offices in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Lebanon to support our regional growth.

    2017

  • Marked our Expansion to the African Continent

    Dr Ben took a bold step to introduce the program in Uganda, which was a massive success. Over 100 graduates completed the program within two years, leading to the establishment of the ICF Kampala Chapter. Subsequently, the program was introduced in Nigeria, and CMA is now active across East and West Africa.

    2018

  • Marked our Expansion to the European Continent

    The program was first launched in the UK and Germany and then expanded towards Eastern Europe, starting in Romania, where it gained positive reception and established a local office. CMA became the first coaching academy started in Asia to successfully introduce a coaching program in the European continent.

    2019

content:
Get Real Results, Real Change with our Transformational Approach

It's one thing to talk about change it's a whole other game to ignite it and make it happen.

When people feel stuck, moving forward to create a sustainable impact requires more than just diagnosing problems and finding solutions. It calls for a transformative shift in how they view themselves and interpret the world, opening up new possibilities for what can be achieved.

Our coaching approach, firmly grounded in transformative learning principles, empowers you to be a powerful catalyst for change.

“ This deep learning experience enhances problem-solving skills and boosts adaptability. When individuals engage in meaningful conversations, they open themselves to new perspectives. This shift allows for a more thoughtful approach to their actions and choices."

" To deliver impactful, sustainable results, your approach must be informed by human psychology combined with proven and tested practical applications. "

A Whole New Approach to Coaching People for Change

Most people understand coaching is about helping people find their solution to move from Point A to Point B. This presumes that the change process is not linear. What if they must navigate complex thoughts, behaviours, and emotions before reaching their goals? That's where conventional coaching falls short.

Having a Solution, and not experience a change, is NOT Good Enough

Now, with our revolutionary transformational approach, which fuses the science and art of coaching.

  • You confidently enhance your ability to engage in person-centric conversations while effectively addressing specific needs and goals.
  • You develop a flexible coaching style that adapts to each individual, encouraging a unique and responsive dialogue.
  • You get better at engaging people in thought-provoking conversations that invite deep reflection.
"When you start to reflect on what you believe and think differently, you open yourself up to questioning what you've always accepted. This helps you discover new ideas and understand yourself and the world better."
  • Take your coaching skills to the next level with the Transformational Approach.
  • This is where science meets coaching - the perfect combination for successful change transformations.

content:
Not All Coaching Programs are Created the Same

When seeking a professional coaching certification, coach training course, or coaching education to enhance your skillset and elevate your confidence and effectiveness, it's essential to consider several key factors beyond just the affordability of the course fee. A holistic approach will help you make the best personal and professional development decisions.

Internationally Recognized Certification

A Professional Coaching Certification that meets rigorous academic standards.

The International Coaching Federation (ICF) is the leading global organisation dedicated to advancing coaching standards and practices and regulating coaching practices. Our coaching program has been approved by the prestigious International Coaching Federation (ICF) and endorsed by Alexandra University in Romania as part of their Master’s Programme in Organizational Coaching.

Our accolades, including being named "Best Coaching Impact" by the ICF, "Best Coach Training Provider” in APAC, and “Best Education Provider,” reflect our commitment to setting high standards and leading the coaching industry.

With our internationally recognised certification, you can confidently embark on your coaching journey, knowing that you are equipped with a qualification that meets academic standards and is approved by the International Coaching Federation (ICF).

Coaching Methodology

Bridging Coaching with Science A Proprietary Coaching Framework for Success

We are pioneering a new frontier in the coaching industry with a transformational approach that is backed by science. Our proprietary coaching approach redefines conventional methods, blending human psychology with coaching psychology to inspire meaningful change in every conversation. This distinctive framework empowers us to stand out in the coaching field.

You gain credibility and confidence in facilitating a meaningful change conversation.

Join us and become part of a pioneering movement shaping the future of coaching through science-based practices.

Comprehensive Training Design

Well-Structured Instructional Design focusing on competency development

Unlike most coaching training courses that offer circumlunar learning, our program follows a deliberate, phased learning approach.

The program comprises various labs designed to help participants become skilled practitioners. Each lab has a unique focus and purpose to provide a well-rounded learning experience - from grasping core concepts to real-world application. Each learning phase is meticulously designed to support you in delivering a transformational impact in your coaching intervention.

The Learning Lab aims to improve and deepen your understanding of the application. You will explore the theoretical frameworks that underpin the methodology while identifying the factors that enhance the effectiveness of the principles involved.

The Competency Lab is designed to help bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge learned in the classroom and practical application. This initiative focuses on hands-on methods, showing you how you can effectively apply the concepts.

The Practical Lab enhances understanding of the methodology by using real-world case studies to effectively demonstrate its application. You will gain valuable practical expertise, enabling you to confidently and proficiently initiate coaching efforts.

The Mentoring Lab, alongside the Practical Lab, offers personalized, detailed feedback from a qualified Coach Supervisor. This customized mentorship aims to enhance your skills and deepen your understanding of the methodology, supporting advanced learning and application of the approach.

The Enrichment Lab provides you with a unique opportunity to observe live demonstrations led by our Master Coaches. They will showcase their expertise in managing complex real-world situations. This hands-on learning platform allows for a deeper understanding and skill development that goes beyond traditional classroom instruction.

Continual Professional Development

Unwavering dedication to Your Developmental Growth

Choosing a coaching education provider is more than just obtaining a qualification. At CMA, our commitment to your formative development is a cornerstone of our coaching education, ensuring that your ongoing development extends well beyond our formal training.

We help you grow through enriching learning opportunities and ensure you have the support and community you need to thrive in your coaching career and practice.

  • Weekly Enrichment Learning
    These sessions present a powerful opportunity to observe live coaching demonstrations by our Master Coaches, showcasing advanced techniques in real scenarios and significantly enhancing practical understanding beyond traditional classrooms.
  • Masterclass
    Explore the exciting world of human science with our masterclasses. Designed to enhance your knowledge and skills, these sessions keep you abreast of the latest trends and developments in coaching practices.
  • Retreat & Conference
    A successful coach must prioritise their well-being. Our retreats & conferences provide a sanctuary for rejuvenation and personal growth, enhancing the skills needed to support clients effectively.
Ever-Expanding Global - Local Support Community

We Are an Active, Thriving Community

Joining Coach Masters Academy means being a part of our global community of passionate practitioners dedicated to personal and organisational transformation. As coach practitioners, we focus not only on guiding others but also on our growth. This thriving community enhances your journey of self-improvement, providing support and inspiration from experienced coaches and like-minded individuals.

  • You can have invaluable opportunities for peer learning, sharing best practices, and collaboration for business opportunities.
  • You will have a supportive network that fosters resilience and prevents burnout, which are crucial factors in maintaining a coach's effectiveness and longevity.

In essence, a vibrant coaching community is not just a nice to have but an essential component in a coach's journey where you can renew their passion and expand your network to learn, grow and contribute meaningfully.

title: Professional & Executive Coaching CertificationCourses
description: Offers core training for professional and executive coaching certification by the panel of expert coaches. Develop your coaching skills and accelerate your knowledge!
content:
A Deep and Focused Conversation

This 90 seconds video presentation explains how our proprietary coaching framework Awareness-Clarity-Choice Conversation enable the change that is deep & sustainable.

A commitment to help leaders and coaches to create change that is deep and sustainable is at the core of our coach training.

Achieved through a process of heightening awareness and deepening learning, this differs from other coaching methodologies that employ a tactical or remedial approach, more useful in troubleshooting or problem-solving. Through deep and focused coaching conversations, a shift from contextual-awareness to self-awareness is created, uncovering how meaning is constructed.

The result: A greater understanding of what matters and how that aligns with what they truly want. Armed with this emerging understanding, a clear path is created, along with the ability to hold themselves accountable to what they want to achieve.

Program Accreditation

The International Coach Federation (ICF), the world-renowned organisation that sets professional coaching industry standards has approved the program. Our Transformational Coaching Program offers a new and powerful approach not seen until now.

With its fresh, leading-edge approach, our process enables authentic, lasting change. Upon completion of the training, you will receive professional coaching certification.

As an academy graduate, you would have gained 70 hours of coach training and satisfied the credentialing requirements, which will enable you to apply for ICF Membership and Credentials.

This certification program does not include the mentor coaching required by ICF for credential application; our academy provides a bundle package for the certification program and mentor coaching.

70 Hours Coach Training Hours

Duration: 16 Weeks

Format: 100% Online

Professional coaching course is designed to build and improve your coaching effectiveness so that you can effectively coach individuals or groups. Coaches who have professional coaching certification are highly skilled that allows them to help their clients improve their lives, relationships and business performance. 


This Certification Program will help you

Acquire the coaching competencies to create powerful perspective shift

Access to a globally platform and be connected with coaches across 5 different continents

Accelerate your professional development with an international recognized coaching certification

Create sustainable change in your team, organization, or community.

Grow your organization’s capacity for change by applying the science of Positive Psychology

Inspire positive change to empower people take small, decisive forward actions

Schedule an appointment with us, TODAY

Our Program Consultants are ICF Credentialed Coaches and they are always available to walk you through the certification training process and the credential roadmap.

This Certification Program will help you.

  • Transformative Coaching Fundamentals

    Coaching is distinctive and set apart from other interventions because it is based solely on the needs of the person being coached, and it uses a clearly defined process throughout the interaction. Both a science and an art, coaching helps people develop potential that is already present but not yet fully manifested.

    • Understanding how coaching is different from consulting, training and counselling
    • Learn when to apply tactical and transformative coaching
    • Understand how coaching evokes excellence in others through horizontal and vertical learning
    • Apply the power of noticing to encourage reflective learning
    • Learn the formula for Sustainability: Alignment + Action + Accountability
    • Acquire a new paradigm shift from a solving mindset to a creating mindset
    • Moving Forward: Roadmap to ICF Credential
  • Engaging in Deep and Focused Conversation

    The coaching conversation is a special conversation. As the primary vehicle for the coach to deliver the coaching, it is a conversation in which the Coach is speaking and listening with a total commitment to helping a person to succeed. This is the most crucial module where students learn how to create a safe psychological space for their client to articulate what is known, but unknown to their conscious mind.

    • Understand what makes a coaching conversation a special conversation.
    • Apply the dynamic flow concept to create a learning conversation
    • Understand coaching presence as the key ingredient to initiate the change process
    • Learn the principles to nurture coaching presence
    • Learn how to create the NOWmoment for the coach and the client
    • Learn how to shift a tactical or remedial conversation to a learning conversation
    • Learn how to exercise active listening to mine the content in the story for a powerful shift in thinking
  • Coaching Dynamic for a Transformative Shift

    The catalyst for change begins at this level, where the client starts to gain more awareness into their current reality and deepen their learning. The student will gain an in-depth understanding of how to use our proprietary framework Awareness-Clarity-Choice ConversationTM to create a conversation aimed at heightening the awareness and deepening the learning.

    • Understand what awareness is and apply the transformative principles to enable a shift in perspective and challenge forward action
    • Learn how to engage in an Awareness Conversation and acquire the coaching skill to explore meaningfulness and frame the conversation for focus effectively
    • Learn how to engage in a Clarity Conversation and acquire proprietary transformative techniques to create the space for self-expression, expand the thoughts for deeper understanding, surface blockages, create current reality and preferred realty
    • Learn how to engage in Choice Conversation and acquire the coaching skills to create support structures to hold people true to their decision and commitment.
  • The Power of Inquiry

    Asking appropriate and powerful questions provides an opportunity to open up new perspectives. This helps to direct our attention to areas that we have not yet considered, enabling us to gain a new understanding through thoughtful thinking. Coaches help their clients to find their solutions through powerful asking.

    • Discover the power of questions and
    • Learn how to structure question for maximum impact
    • Understand the framework for meta-coaching
    • Avoid making the top 8 mistakes when asking questions
    • Learn how to ask empowering questions
  • Integrating Core Competencies

    A coaching conversation is more than a dialogue session or a friendly chat. The objective of a coaching conversation is to facilitate positive change in how a person thinks, acts or feels. In this module, you will learn how to integrate the ICF Core Competencies.

    • Establishing Coaching Goals
    • Co-Creating the Relationship
    • Effective Communication 
    • Forward Action

title: Program Structure for Career Development and Transition Coaching-Coach Masters Academy
content:
A Progressive, Flexible Roadmap to earning the Dual Certification Click here for more information on the Transformative Core Training After you have completed the Transformative Core Training for Professional Coaching, we provide an add-on module applying the transformative principles in career coaching.
  •   Module A: Conceptual Framework for Career Success

    The pursuit of happiness is an important goal for many people. However, surprisingly little scientific research has focused on how happiness can be increased and sustained in career transition coaching. Many people are quite accomplished in their chosen fields. However, simply having these achievements does not necessarily lead to career success. 

    This module provides an empirical basis for career coaching, by examining the conceptual framework on the psychology of work and how the science of Positive Psychology can enrich approaches to career guidance, development, and transition.

    Part 1 Career Matter: Leveraging on Positive Psychology Working toward a fulfilling career is a long-term, continual development process. When you fail to intentionally become something, you unintentionally become anything, and that “anything” often leads to significant unhappiness. Helping you align your intention with your value and purpose is key to finding fulfilment at work. Using the PERMA model of flourishing, we explore the principal determinants of career success and discuss how the model can support you in finding alignment and achievement. This series of learning includes the following: ● Understanding the Science of Happiness at Work ● Defining and Measuring Career Success ● Applying the PERMA Model Part 2 Increase Adaptability Competency  It is no surprise that, in a constantly changing world, adaptability is a crucial ingredient for career success. The “adaptability competency” means having flexibility in handling change, juggling multiple demands, and adapting to new situations with fresh ideas or innovative approaches. Applying self-efficacy theory as part of the coaching process can help develop, improve, and enhance your adaptability competency. Part 3 The Role of a Career Coach As Career Coach, we take on multiple roles in helping our clients map their career development and pathways.  In this section, we take a closer look at these roles and how the science applies to them - being a successful and effective career coach and helping our client to find career success and satisfaction.
    Career Compass   Partner with clients to gain insight of self and focus on the client’s cause
    Career Capital   Partner with client to review their internal assets and explore what are their available social capital resources
    Career Capability   Engage the client to stand boldly and moving forward to build their possible career
  •   Module B - Mastering the Career Coaching Competencies

    In mastering career coaching competencies, it is essential to be able to infuse/display the understanding of career development theories and the skilful applications of career development tools. Your coaching process is the foundation of your ability to help clients. Therefore, in this module, we will integrate career development theories, models, and tools into a coaching framework, to prepare coaches for a robust and effective coaching process.

    Part 1 Coaching Model and Framework for Career Development Career Development Models and Frameworks is the science that makes a career coaching process framework robust. By integrating career development theories into the coaching process, this will ignite an emerging mindset and create a generative change. ● Traits and Factors Theory ● Developmental Theory ● Transitional Theory ● Postmodern Theory Part 2 Assessment Tools / Psychometric Tool Career Assessment Tools play an important role in any career coaching process.  They act as a catalyst to gain self-awareness, an approach that’s backed by scientific credibility.  A good understanding and application of the theory and components supporting the tools will be crucial in your coaching process. In this part, we will explore: ● RIASEC tool ● Career Adapt-Abilities Scale ● Career Projector Part 3 A Dialogic Coaching Process: Helping Skill for Career Guidance Most career coaching conversations are geared towards a dialectical method.  However, to manage more sustainable change, it’s preferable to have a more dialogic coaching process, invoking a search and understanding of the self as well as the situation. In this module, we will be leveraging CMA's ACC framework, integrating career development theories, tools, and models into a dialogic coaching process. ● Challenge and ignite the innovation, creativity and innovation of the client ● Address the impact of and provide help with the management of job loss/transition
  •   Module C - Integration A deeper discussion and study to integrate the concepts and processes of a dialogic coaching conversation is very much needed, to create understanding and develop competencies.  In this module, we will facilitate discussions and learnings using case studies, in the application of an ACC conversation Part 1 Application of the ACC Conversation for Career Coaching Special attention on how to keep people making progress while developing the next steps after they achieve their goals, as well as how to inspire them to take on new challenges and look to the future with excitement and enthusiasm. Part 2 Case Study Uniquely real-life case studies in career coaching, commonly encountered by career coaches, to facilitate learning and proficiency in coaching competencies.

To receive the Global Career Development Facilitator certification, you only need to complete 106 hours of online training.

This can be done entirely at your own pace and schedule.

  •   Module 1 Workforce and Career Development History • Define workforce development and how it differs from education and economic development • History and structure of the workforce development system • Role of the career services provider • Intake interviews
  •   Module 2 Ethics and Career Services Provider • Definition and importance of a professional code of ethics for career services providers • Methods for deciding if a career services provider is operating within the scope of their training and job responsibilities • Ethical decision-making strategies • Personal and professional values impact ethical decision-making • Process for ethical decision-making • Role boundaries in ethical decision-making
  •   Module 3 Career Development Theory • Review key career development theories, models, and techniques and apply them to the client you serve • Define terms: Occupation, Job, Career, Career Development, Career Counseling, Assistance, Guidance & Planning Process • Steps in the career development process • Understanding the importance of career choice and development theory • Limitations of career choice and development theories

title: THE POWER OF “PURE” COACHING PROCESS-Coach Masters Academy
content:
The growth of professional coaching worldwide generates a diverse understanding among coaching clients about what coaching is and what it isn’t. We believe that in order for clients to receive the full impact of coaching as defined by ICF, Coaches are required to take a stronger stance for the power of “pure” coaching.

When coaches steadfastly commit to deliver the coaching process to our clients without blending it with other modalities such as consulting or counseling, we too more deeply experience and appreciate “pure” coaching’s power. As we draw out the client’s wisdom and provide access to as-yet-unknown approaches to the situations and topics being explored within the coaching relationship, client awareness unleashes latent potential and innate creativity better than any other human development modality.
In this article, we will be sharing with you four key elements that make the “pure” coaching process powerful in its own right. These three elements are: (1) Trust in the Process, (2) Copious Curiosity, and (3) Risk Taking.

Invitation to Exploration:

  • During your upcoming coaching sessions, notice at which point(s) you find yourself not trusting the “pure” coaching process.
  • As you notice it, what do you find yourself thinking?
  • What beliefs, attitudes or experiences underlie those thoughts, prompting you to insert your own knowledge, expertise or viewpoint?
  • Experiment with the “pure” coaching process and notice the degree of commitment and follow-through you witness with your client.
Trust in Progress

The ICF defines coaching as:
“Coaching is partnering with clients in a thought-provoking and creative process that inspires them to maximize their personal and professional potential.”

One dictionary definition of ‘process’ is, “a systematic series of actions directed to some end.” The ICF coaching competencies represent the systematic series of actions of the “though-provoking and creative process that inspires…” and the ‘end’ to which these actions are directed is, “…to maximize their personal and professional potential.”

Within the “pure” coaching process defined by the coaching competencies, a professional Coach:

  1. Is in integrity with the coaching ethics and standards,
  2. Co-creates clear agreements with clients (including individual session agreements),
  3. Provides an environment of trust and intimacy,
  4. Stays fully present in each moment,
  5. Actively listens,
  6. Asks powerful questions, and
  7. Uses direct communication, all of which contributes to
  8. Creating awareness, from which actions are designed,
  9. Plans and goals for those actions are set, and
  10. Progress and accountability are measured.

Throughout the entire coaching process the client is capable and resourceful and that the Coach fully believes that to be true and interact with the client accordingly. Most importantly, the client is not being pushed. Instead there is complete trust in the client to choose wisely. The Coach is consistently available for what is and what shows up in each moment, confident to perceive what is most important and respond to it authentically. The Coach surrenders to the flow and momentum created in the reciprocal field between client and coach that occurs through the process of “pure” coaching. 

Copius Curiosity

One of the more common statements we hear from coaches is, “My clients expect me to know and to tell them what I know.” When you enter into a relationship with a client with this premise as an expectation, you enter into a consulting relationship, a relationship based on you as expert rather than equal peer, not a coaching one. Remember, the definition of coaching describes a “thought-provoking and creative process.” What is thought-provoking or creative about telling someone what is already known?

Referring again to the core coaching competencies, it states that “the coach is comfortable not knowing as one of the best states to expand awareness in.” “The coach evidences a complete curiosity that is undiluted by a need to perform.” and, “the coach’s questions are fully based in curiosity and the coach does not ask questions to which the coach knows the answer.”

Cultivating a state of copious curiosity means a willingness to TRULY not know; to set aside everything you think you know and to ask questions that can elicit what the client knows or solutions that are completely unique to the client and the client’s situation. This precludes asking leading questions, those to which you are attached to or know the answer; in other words, there are no conditions on the questions you pose nor a preconceived outcome expected.

This state of curiosity asks you, as coach, to be spontaneous, to be bold and to revere not knowing for both you and your client. By doing so, you can effortlessly invite, solicit and draw out from the client new awareness, clarity, and solutions which emerge from the exchange between you rather than from history.

Copious curiosity is a space in which you and your client can celebrate mystery and wonder about everything without needing to know why. It’s a space of innovation, creativity and unlimited exploration that can yield surprising and impactful insights.

Invitation to Exploration:

  • During upcoming coaching sessions, notice at which point(s) you find yourself allowing your own experience, beliefs, attitudes or knowledge to block your ability to be copiously curious.
  • As you notice it, what do you find yourself thinking and doing?
  • Having identified those thoughts, how can you choose to return to copious curiosity?
Risk Taking

Risk taking here refers to the client’s ability to express their greatness. It also serves to create awareness that has not yet been explored. A Coach should not be afraid of asking questions that will make either him/ her or the client or both uncomfortable.

When a coach consistently trusts the process of “pure” coaching and explores with a client from copious curiosity, the opportunities for risk taking become obvious. Coach and client attune more easily, and openly access and name what is seen, heard, sensed and felt in the space between you and the client. In other words, the Coach and the client take comfort in the discomfort of the unknown and facilitate fresh breakthroughs.

The synergy of multiple ways of perceiving generates permission to see, hear, sense, feel, relate to and share everything being experienced in the exchange; the wholeness of the situation in which everything matters is clearly evident. Within this space, client assumptions, perspectives and beliefs can be challenged; you can both dive deeply into any incongruity, inconsistency, incoherency or paradox inherent in the situation or conversation.

By being willing to tell the truth as it emerges, freedom from self-protection is available because it’s no longer required. When you, as coach, model risk taking with and for the client they gain full permission to reciprocate and do the same, opening richer and deeper avenues of exploration. New awareness is a natural by-product of risk taking.


Invitation to Exploration:

  • During upcoming coaching sessions, notice at which point(s) you hesitate to be bold or take a risk in service to your client.
  • As you notice it, what do you find yourself thinking and doing?
  • What will support you to develop ease and comfort with taking risks in service to client awareness?

The growth of professional coaching worldwide generates a diverse understanding among coaching clients about what coaching is and what it isn’t. We believe that in order for clients to receive the full impact of coaching as defined by ICF, Coaches are required to take a stronger stance for the power of “pure” coaching.

title: Tips for when to coach-Coach Masters Academy
content:
• Coach employees who are aware of a performance problem or skill gap and who are motivated to address the situation.
  • Don’t expect to solve a problem in a single coaching session. Coaching is an ongoing process.
  • Coach informally “on-the-spot” as you overhear a conversation or observe a specific behavior that indicates a potential performance problem or skill gap.
  • Offer coaching if you see a need—but first explain what you’ve observed and why you think coaching would be valuable.
  • Don’t try to force coaching on someone who doesn’t want to improve or who isn’t aware that he or she has a performance problem.
  • Avoid coaching if unproductive behavior is deeply rooted and occurs across a broad range of situations. Such problems usually don’t clear up with coaching.
  • Find opportunities to strengthen your coaching skills. Regular practice improves a coach’s effectiveness.
Tips for Effective Coaching
  • Create an atmosphere of trust. Trust makes coaching possible, and the act of coaching strengthens trust.
  • Keep the coaching focused to one or two goals that will help the employee improve performance or close a skill gap.
  • Cultivate a comfortable setting during coaching sessions. Make sure you will not be interrupted. Set a positive tone, and communicate genuine support for the person’s development.
  • Establish ground rules up front. For example, what is said during a coaching session will remain confidential, and each party will agree to fulfill his or her commitments to the coaching process.
  • Establish preferred work styles and a method of feedback up front. For instance, some people like to receive feedback in written form so they can process it at their own pace and refer to it during the coaching process. Others prefer to receive feedback in spoken form.
  • Set mini-milestones to help your coachee build confidence and stay motivated.
  • Be clear about who has promised what during the coaching process. To maintain accountability, periodically assess whether both parties have fulfilled their agreements and commitments.
  • For large goals, such as acquiring a new skill, invite your coachee to create an action plan that lays out the coaching need, the goal, the steps the coachee will take to achieve the goal, ways of reviewing progress, and the role that the coach will play (for example, attending meetings to observe the coachee’s behavior).
Tips for Giving Feedback
  • Give feedback as soon as possible after observing performance. Wait only if doing so is necessary to gather necessary information. On the other hand, if the behavior you’ve observed was particularly upsetting, consider waiting until you’ve calmed down before providing feedback.
  • Don’t use feedback simply to underscore poor performance. Also provide feedback on work that is done well—you’ll help your employee learn from what he or she did right.
  • Focus feedback on behavior, not character or personality. Emphasizing behavior helps prevent the other person from feeling personally attacked.
  • Avoid generalizations. Instead of saying, “You did a great job during the meeting,” offer feedback that is more specific, such as “The graphics in your presentation really communicated the message.”
  • Describe the other person’s behavior and its impact on projects and/or coworkers. You’ll help the person see why it’s important to address problem behavior.
  • Focus feedback on factors that the other person can control. Feedback on factors that he or she cannot control is not constructive.
  • Keep feedback focused on issues that your employee can rework or improve in the future.
  • If a troubling behavior or action was a one-time event, consider letting it go.
  • Be sincere. Give feedback with the clear intent of helping the person improve.
  • Give feedback as often as necessary.
Tips for Receiving Feedback
  • Ask your direct report for specific information about how the coaching process is going. “What did I say that made you think I wasn’t interested in your proposal?” or “How were my suggestions helpful to you?”
  • Ask for clarification in ways that don’t make your coachee defensive. “Could you give me an example?”—not “What do you mean, I was unreceptive to your idea?”
  • Help your coachee avoid emotion-laden terms. “You said that I’m often inflexible. Give me an example of things I do that give you this sense.”
  • Don’t be defensive. Offer justification or commentary on your actions only if asked. Tell your coachee when you’ve gotten all the feedback you can process.
  • Thank the person for his or her feedback, positive and negative. You’ll build trust and model productive behavior.
Steps for Reaching Agreement

  1. Inquire into and advocate different perspectives.

    Throughout the coaching process, you and your coachee need to agree on goals, create plans for achieving them, and make any changes necessary to improve the coaching process. A blend of inquiry and advocacy can help.

    For example, “Julie, I’d really like to see you build the skills you need to take leadership of the product development team. Based on what I’ve observed, and what you’ve told me, learning to delegate would be a major challenge for you as a new manager. What do you see as the most important focus for our coaching sessions?”

  2. Present proposals.

    Offer your ideas for conducting the coaching process or helping your employee achieve his or her goals.

    For instance, “Julie, I think that talking with several experienced managers about delegating could be very helpful.”

  3. Check for understanding.

    Ask questions to assess your employee’s understanding of what you’re proposing.

    “Julie, what is your understanding of the delegating process? In your view, how will we measure your progress with this skill?”

  4. Check for agreement.

    Ask questions to check whether you and your coachee are in agreement.

    “Julie, do we agree, then, that our coaching should focus on delegating skills rather than another aspect of management?”

  5. Revisit step 1 when agreement is in question and begin the process again.

    If you check for agreement and the employee’s response indicates lack of agreement, begin blending inquiry with advocacy again. The following dialogue provides an example:

    Coach: “Julie, do we agree that we’ll review your progress on delegating in two months, and that we’ll measure your progress according to whether you’ve met your goal of delegating four projects to team members?”

    Julie: “I’m a little nervous about having just two months. I’ve got another big deadline that will hit midway through that timeframe, and I’m not sure I can handle the coaching assignment at the same time.”

    Coach: “I think it’s important to review your progress on the delegating assignment promptly, and I’m worried that waiting longer than two months may make it harder for you to learn this skill. Do you share my concern? If so, let’s explore ideas for sticking with that timetable.”

    Julie: “If the two-month review is crucial, maybe I could reduce the number of delegated projects to three instead of four. That might be more manageable.”

    Coach: “That sounds like a good idea. So, we’ll agree to review your progress two months from today to see whether you’ve been able to delegate three tasks to your team?”

    Julie: “Yes, let’s move ahead with that understanding.”

Here are some practical tips for when to coach and how to deliver effective coaching engagement.

title: Understanding Transformative Coaching-Coach Masters Academy
content:
Article Interview with our Founder - Understanding the uniqueness of CMA Transformative Coaching

Interview Article: The Chief Editor of Smart Investor catches up with our Founder, Ben Koh an ICF Master Certified Coach (MCC) on his vision to become the catalyst to transform organisation and people through transformative coaching. Find out how coaching contributes to effective leadership that will benefit the organization and how it helps leaders to align to the organization's goal.

Read more

Expand Capacity for Deep Reflective Thinking

Drawing on many years of fieldwork and research, Dr Ben Koh, the founder of Coach Masters Academy, has developed a proprietary transformative coaching framework known as the Awareness-Clarity-Choice (ACC) Conversation. It is an empirical approach that blends the science of Positive Psychology with the theories of transformative learning to support generative change. 

Read more

Distinctiveness of our Transformational Approach

Our transformative coaching offers you a robust framework that can be applied in a wide and diverse context including coaching executives in workplace, leadership effectiveness and development and career-related issues. It can also be used in life coaching for people seeking fulfilment, purpose, meaning and alignment.

Read more

Advancing Human Potential

Professional coaching contributes to advancing human potential because it begins from a deep-seated belief that humans have potential and that this potential can be advanced.

Read more

Wisdom Isn’t What You Think It Is

By David Brooks, Apr 2021

Wise people don’t tell us what to do, they start by witnessing our story. They take the anecdotes, rationalizations and episodes we tell, and see us in a noble struggle. They see our narratives both from the inside, as we experience them, and from the outside, as we can’t. They see the ways we’re navigating the dialectics of life — intimacy versus independence, control versus uncertainty — and understand that our current self is just where we are right now, part of a long continuum of growth.

Read more

title: Value of Coaching-Coach Masters Academy
content:
Coaching works because it taps on the science of Positive Psychology. It is based on a simple principle – focus on the positive gives you positive outcome. William James commented that ” the greatest discovery is that human being can alter his life by altering his attitudes of mind. What makes coaching such a powerful tool for transformation is the use of powerful question that directs the mind to focus on RIGHT source – not so much in problem fixing, but in deepening awareness. When coupled with the science of Positive Psychology it gives people a sense of optimism that can be best summed up in one word – HOPE. 

Effective coaching challenges limiting assumptions embedded in our viewpoints about self and others in a way different than teaching or training. Good teaching and training also challenge the limits of learners, but in a different way — by adding new knowledge and skills … coaching is a unique form of dialogue that expands an individual’s capacity to transform his or her limiting beliefs. William Stockton

We become our best, most powerful selves when we have someone we can count on to reflect back to us, and to hold us accountable to, our emotions and thoughts, our hidden brilliance, our barriers and obstacles, and our secret, infinite capacity for accomplishment. Once we tap into our own inner strengths, then creativity, progress and accomplishment follow accordingly. Hilary Weber

title: Webinar-Coach Masters Academy
content:
A Shift from Diagnosis to Discovery: Rethink I Redefine Professional Coaching 22 Jul , 12:00 AM Singapore Register Now

The late John Whitmore, esteemed as the Father of Professional Coaching, rightly pointed out that coaching is helping people to learn rather than find solutions. It is a co-creative process where people find the thinking space for reflection. In doing so, they gain a new understanding of their own experiences, enabling them to be more choice-ful about their decision.

In this webinar, the panel of speakers will help you appreciate the distinctiveness of professional coaching by unveiling some of the incomplete understanding. At the same time, they will share from their experiences:
- What is the benchmark to measure the success of a coaching engagement?
- If change is good, why is it not happening?
- Why helping the client to think about their solution is not good enough?

A Transformational Team Coaching approach for alignment 11 May , 11:00 PM Singapore Register Now

This webinar explores how team coaching can shift "I" to "We" culture.

In today's highly competitive business environment, teams are critical to organizational success. However, achieving and maintaining team alignment is an ongoing challenge that requires HR leaders' continual attention. To help teams learn collectively from their successes and failures, optimize their performance, and adapt quickly to changing demands, there are a few strategies that HR leaders can implement.

In this 60 min webinar, we examine how HR Leaders through team coaching, help teams become more aligned, foster greater collaboration and trust among team members, increase motivation and engagement levels, and create a stronger sense of purpose.

What can you expect to learn from this webinar?

  1. What are the constructs of team alignment through the 5C Model.
  2. How to activate Alignment through connected conversations.
  3. Learn the role of a team coach in the co-creating alignment of teams.

title: Webinar-Coach Masters Academy
content:
AI Coach or Human Coach? 13 Mar 2024 13 Mar , 03:00 PM Singapore Register Now

As we move further into the digital age, the impact of AI can be seen in various areas of human life, including the growing profession of coaching. Many argue that AI has limitations, especially regarding human intelligence and emotions. This raises doubts about AI's ability to compete with a human coach. Are you sure about this?

Recent studies on the application of AI in mental health care have suggested that AI could effectively promote human well-being. This improved ability of AI and its increased use in the helping professions challenges us to reassess the distinctive quality of our coaching conversations.

For the foreseeable future, AI will remain unconscious machines that can, at best, support humans in complex, specific tasks. So, this webinar invites us to a thoughtful dialogue to

(1) examine the essence of a coaching conversation as a human story unfolding to reveal where positive change needs to be and

(2) Advocate an urgent need to employ a more science-based approach to create personal change.

The agenda for the presentation is as follows:

1. Review two case studies showcasing AI's successful use in mental health intervention.
2. Examine the AI-human interaction in a coaching context.
3. Review a comparative study of a coaching conversation between an AI coach and a human coach.
4. Map out potential future directions for professional coaching.


This webinar will NOT be recorded. You must attend the live session to enjoy the learning.

content:
Applying a transformational coaching approach in Shadow Work 19 Oct , 08:00 PM Singapore Register Now

You can expect to walk away from this webinar with a holistic understanding of dealing with negative emotions and resistance during a coaching session.

Coaching is widely accepted as professional development and performance enhancement for workplace coaching. While many coaching clients usually seek focused solutions to immediate problems or challenges, it is not uncommon for deep-seated issues or resistance and reluctance to deal with them to show up during the coaching session.

In this learning webinar, Dr Ben Koh advocates a dynamic alliance between transformational and psychotherapy approaches that can facilitate a mutual and more purposeful change process to support your clients to embrace their shadows. Of particular interest is the role of critical reflection in the adult learning theories and awareness in Gestalt Therapy in the transformative process of creating deep and sustainable change.

What you can expect from the webinar:
• Wholeness is not faultless: Why work with shadow experience?
• 4 Practical Tips on how to work with shadow using a transformational approach

 Dr Ben Koh I Master Certified Coach

title: Webinar-Coach Masters Academy
content:
Applying a Transformative Framework in Workplace Coaching 20 Oct , 12:00 AM Singapore Register Now

In this webinar, you will understand the parameters that define Executive Coaching and what inputs should be considered when paired with CMA’s Transformative Coaching Framework. By the end of the session, you can define your executive coaching offering and how that intersects with executives, their work, their teams, and their organizations.

title: Webinar-Coach Masters Academy

Awareness of Brain-Wiring 12 May , 08:00 AM Singapore Register Now

Don't miss out on this valuable opportunity to gain an in-depth understanding of the impact of brain-wiring on coaching and learn how to become a better coach by leveraging the power of brain-wiring!

Coaching is a process that involves communication, and the cognitive differences between men and women can influence communication. 

While the findings of studies on the effects of these differences are still inconclusive, new research has yielded evidence of the inherent differences in how men's and women's brains are neurologically wired.

Research has also found that men and women use different parts of their brains when processing information. 

Men predominantly use the left side of their brain, responsible for logic, analysis, and linear thinking. 

In contrast, women use both sides of their brains, which allows for a more integrated and holistic approach to problem-solving. 

This difference can be significant in coaching, as coaches need to have a flexible approach that can accommodate the different thinking styles of their clients.

This discovery has important implications for coaching.

Having an awareness of these differences may enhance our coaching perspectives and processes.

It can help coaches better understand their clients' communication styles, emotional needs, and thinking processes, leading to more effective coaching outcomes. 

By being mindful of these differences, coaches can create a more inclusive coaching environment that can accommodate the diverse needs of their clients.

The webinar will explore these studies in more depth and discuss strategies coaches can use to better integrate this knowledge into their practice. 

Presented by CMA USA Team

content:
Bridging the Science to the Art of coaching 16 May , 12:00 AM Singapore Register Now

Is Coaching a Science or an Art?

In this keynote speech, Dr Ben wants to bridge the gap and explore and value of science in the coaching process. As a thought leader in transformative coaching, he sees coaching conversation as an artwork where coaches master their craft to inquire powerfully to evoke greater awareness, clarity and understanding.

It is often theorized that there is a conflict between science and coaching, where coaching is postulated as an art. Henceforth, whether coaching is a science or art is fraught because it suggests that science and art are diametrically opposites. This tendency to dichotomize is stubbornly pervasive in human thought. Neither does accepting coaching as both science and art help clarify how the coaching process is a change process.

The term science can also refer to scientific thinking, where we use the principles of evidence, logic, and reason to explain and understand things around us. Carl Sagan put it well when he said, " science is a way of thinking much more than a body of knowledge. "While it is true that there are many "soft skills" involved in coaching, good practice must include an evidence base and the use of scientific thinking.

In this 90 mins presentation, Dr Ben will speak on the following aspects:

① The concept of change is at the heart of coaching: How the theory of transformative learning bridges the science to the art of coaching

② What are the essential components in the coaching process to create lasting impact beyond the coaching session

③ The future of coaching as a profession: What lies ahead for the continuing professional development of aspiring coaches

In this webinar, the panel of speakers will unveil key differences between wearing a "Manager" hat versus a "Coaching hat" and share some key pointers on how a Leader can build, sharpen, and elevate their coaching capabilities. 

According to an article in the Harvard Business Review, "coaching is an essential tool for achieving business goals" (2015).  Coaching develops the organization's people and in turn, allows them to deliver their business goals in support of the organizational business goals.  As Leaders (or Managers), the coaching tool is simply part of the toolbox that great Leaders carry.  Building this tool, sharpening it, and knowing when to use it, all elevate a Leader's ability to engage their teams and stakeholders effectively.

Some critical questions answered will be:

  • What outcome does a manager hat versus a coaching hat drive to?
  • In what instances does it best serve to wear which hat?
  • How does an organization benefit from coaching leaders?
  • How is this applied in real businesses corporately as an offering to support the growth of leaders?
  • What can a Leader consider in building and sharpening this tool?

Core Competency: Trust and Intimacy I Active Listening

This can also be defined by the competency of "Creating Trust and Intimacy", the ability to create a safe, supportive environment that produces ongoing mutual respect and trust. 

By applying active listening as a leader, with the ability to focus completely on what the team member is saying and is not saying, understand the meaning of what is said in the context of the team member's desires, and support the team member's self-expression through a current situation to support the organization's objectives.  This will help the leader support their team member beyond a transactional conversation to better the team to transform in performance and business outcomes.

Are we heading in the Right Direction? Does coaching provide a return on its investment in driving performance and impacting the bottom line? To answer this question, we must reflect on how coaching addresses developmental learning in today’s context.

Successful organisations in the emerging knowledge economy innovate continually to maintain their place in a dynamic marketplace. Leaders must develop agility and creativity to drive growth and deliver results.

title: Webinar-Coach Masters Academy
content:
Learning from Silence: Creating Space for Creativity to Thrive 17 May , 12:00 AM Singapore Register Now

In this webinar, you will discover how to merge imagination and reality and learn a new tool to evoke learning in any situation. You will walk away appreciating how you can apply this simple approach to carry out everyday coaching conversation that is rich and meaningful. Jaques, an Agile Coach, working in the video-gaming industry, understands perfectly why speech is silver and silence is gold. Drawing from his journey, where his work enables his team to innovate and come out with a new, fresh idea, he wants to share how you can be the canvas for someone else's creativity by tapping into the power of silence.

Are you afraid of silence?

Yet, we know there is so much power we can tap into when there is silence.

Somewhere we know that without silence, words lose their meaning. Henri Nouwen

Creative thinking intentionally gainsnew insights and different ideas through existing information. Creative thought often involves tapping into different thinking styles and examining information from different viewpoints to see new patterns.            

The good news is this - anyone can foster a creative mind when you learn how to harness the power of generative listening, which is at the core of our transformational coaching approach.

Speaker: Jaques Smit, Professional Certified Coach

title: Webinar-Coach Masters Academy
content:
" Letting Go of Nothing " by Susan Andah 01 Feb , 08:00 PM Singapore Register Now

In this learning webinar, you will learn 2 lessons to help you be more present, calmer, and find inner peace. (1) Letting In and (2) Letting Be.

Struggling to let go is often because we refuse to see the situation differently.

The word “relax” means to “be loose again,” but we cannot achieve this by tightening our muscles, physically or mentally. Letting go is not something we can force, even if we try hard. We cannot simply think away our grievances, expectations, or attachments.

Instead, we must change our inner landscape and let go naturally. This involves stopping ourselves from holding on.

The second step of letting go is to let be.

Once we fully allow ourselves to feel the pain, we should not attempt to change it or wish it away. Instead, we should accept it and befriend it. Soon, we will notice the experience shifting, even without us doing anything.

Whatever we are experiencing, we should first notice and let it in.

Then, we can let it be. By doing so, we will be able to let it go.

title: Webinar-Coach Masters Academy
content:
Making Change Comes Alive 17 May , 12:00 AM Singapore Register Now

Unpack the science to create a lasting change beyond the coaching session.

This webinar will help you appreciate how understanding the change process as a multidimensional creative process versus a linear process impacts how we facilitate change for ourselves and others and affect the change outcomes.

As much as we want change to happen for ourselves, creating a long-lasting change requires more than defining a set of actions, step one, step two, step three. There is more to deep, lasting change, for we are more than that! 

As human beings, our actions, choices, and responses are based on a construct of ways of thinking, beliefs, values, intentions, and concerns, just to name a few.

Transformational change requires us to see and understand the different aspects of our current operations. Then based on this understanding, we can become choiceful in creating a new way of doing, thinking and feeling, leading to a new way of being.

What you can expect to learn from this webinar:

① We will draw upon the gestalt theory and the biopsychosocial model to illustrate the multilayer dimensions involved in the change process.  

② We will provide an in-depth study on how our proprietary Awareness-Clarity-Choice Conversation integrates these dimensions to evoke greater clarity and understanding.

title: Webinar-Coach Masters Academy
content:
Maximising human potential: The Paradox in One-to-One and Team Coaching 19 May , 12:00 AM Singapore Register Now

In this webinar, we will explore how the principles of coaching the whole person can be related to coaching teams as a system or ‘the whole person. We will be looking at how the team transformation coaching approach recognises the powerful influence that teams have on individuals and not vice-versa and how coaching provides the opportunity to heighten systemic self-awareness.

Professional Coaching in the one-to-one context seeks to maximise human potential through the expansion of the thinking capacity of human beings to provide fulfilling results for sustainable change. Critical skill coaches bring to one-to-one coaching is recognising the ‘person holistically’, with all the components they get into the session as part of their makeup. For the client, we coach wholeness to understand how to construct these different elements into a whole.

This session is particularly beneficial to internal coaches and HR practitioners who usually wonder how best to get more employees to benefit from the coaching intervention. External coaches will also find this helpful in negotiating with contractors and sponsors to have more staff participating, impacting teams beyond the leaders who currently carry the burden of influencing teams when supported by individual Coaching.

Presented by Joan Mugenzi & Abioloa Orojo

title: Webinar-Coach Masters Academy
content:
Mindful Lisetning 24 Nov , 11:00 PM Singapore Register Now

Mindfulness is the capacity to attend to your experiences while also paying attention to your attention. It requires a shift in your awareness to a higher level: seeing yourself from the whole.

The coaches’ capacity to simultaneously pay attention to the client’s narration and the internal listening process of hearing, understanding, remembering, interpreting, evaluating, and responding will decide the quality and effectiveness of the coaching intervention.

In transformative coaching, we support the coachee to open the mind to heighten awareness and deepen the learning for the coachee to choose meaningful forward action.

In creating such a transformative space, a coach needs to develop the capacity to listen to the whole of the coachee's narrated experience.

What can you expect to take away?
1. To Understand what makes mindful listening important in a transformative coaching conversation?
2. What are the benefits of mindful listening in a coaching intervention that facilitates the transformation?
3. To learn some practical tips and contemplative practices that suites you to build capacity as a mindful listener.

Jayathan Fernando
